 \n 
Epstein joked with his brother about his friendship with Woody Allen, emails show
 \n 
 \n  
Emails released by the justice department on Friday show that Jeffrey Epstein joked with his brother Mark about his friendship with Woody Allen in 2012, years after he was first convicted of sex crimes but managed to find his way back into New York society.
 \n  
The partially redacted email exchange, in March 2012, begins with Mark Epstein, using an email address that was revealed as his in another document, asking his brother about the possibility that their parents had sex in the bath when they were children.
 \n  
After Jeffrey Epstein replies \u201cAghhhhhjh\u201d, Mark Epstein asks him where he is.
 \n  
\u201cParis with woody allen\u201d Jeffrey Epstein answers.
 \n  
\u201cFor les pedophile convention?\u201d Mark Epstein asks.
 \n  
\u201ci think pedophiles is the plural\u201d Jeffrey Epstein replies.
 \n  
As CBS News reported last year, previously released records show that Allen and his wife, Soon-Yi Previn, were among Epstein\u2019s most frequent social companions in the years leading up to his death.
 \n  
The records showed nearly 100 instances between 2014 and 2019 in which Allen and Epstein \u2013 almost always joined by Previn \u2014 were scheduled to spend time together.

Epstein files include dozens of documents with Trump's quote calling late sex offender 'a lot of fun to be with'
 \n 
 \n  
The files from the federal investigations into Jeffrey Epstein, the late sex offender who socialized with Donald Trump for more than a decade, include 74 documents that refer to the fact that Trump called Epstein \u201ca lot of fun to be with\u201d in a flattering 2002 New York magazine profile of the financier.
 \n  
\u201cI\u2019ve known Jeff for 15 years. Terrific guy,\u201d Trump told the New York writer Landon Thomas in 2002. \u201cHe\u2019s a lot of fun to be with. It is even said that he likes beautiful women as much as I do, and many of them are on the younger side. No doubt about it \u2013 Jeffrey enjoys his social life.\u201d
 \n  
Trump\u2019s assessment of Epstein appears in the files dozens of times, as prosecutors dug into the disgraced financier, and his accomplice, Ghislaine Maxwell.

 12.34am GMT 
 \n 
Ro Khanna and Thomas Massie demand to see unredacted versions of Epstein files
 \n 
 \n  
Ro Khanna and Thomas Massie, the two congressmen who wrote the Epstein Files Transparency Act, the federal law that requires the justice department to release documents related to the investigations of Jeffrey Epstein, the late sex offender, just sent a letter to Todd Blanche, the deputy attorney general, to demand a meeting to review the unredacted files.
 \n  
\u201cAt a recent news conference, you stated that Members of Congress may arrange to review unredacted versions of the Department\u2019s production,\u201d Khanna, a California Democrat, and Massie, a Kentucky Republican, wrote to Blanche, who was previously Donald Trump\u2019s personal lawyer.
 \n  
\u201cGiven ongoing reported concerns regarding the scope and consistency of redactions in the documents released to date, we respectfully request a meeting to review the unredacted records.\u201d
 \n  
The letter continues:
 \n  
 \n   
In particular, we seek access to the following categories of materials:
 \n   
First, hundreds of thousands of pages of emails and other documents recovered from Jeffrey Epstein\u2019s email accounts during the 2018 and 2019 investigations into Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell.
 \n   
Second, victim interview statements from the initial Florida investigation and subsequent investigations in New York. We understand that the Department possesses FBI Form 302 reports documenting these interviews. However, the materials released to date in this category consist largely of pages that are fully redacted, providing no meaningful information for oversight or public accountability.
 \n   
Third, the 53-page draft indictment and the 82-page prosecution memorandum prepared during the 2007 Florida investigation. These documents are essential to understanding the government\u2019s knowledge of Epstein\u2019s criminal conduct and the circumstances surrounding the non-prosecution agreement and immunity he received.
 \n   
We have seen a blanket approach to redactions in some areas, while in other cases, victim names were not redacted at all. Congress cannot properly assess the Department\u2019s handling of the Epstein and Maxwell cases without access to the complete record.
 \n   
Accordingly, we request your assistance in arranging a secure, in-person review of these unredacted materials at the Department\u2019s earliest convenience.

 12.11am GMT 
 \n 
New files include friendly 2002 email to Ghislaine Maxwell, signed 'Love, Melania'
 \n 
 \n  
The new batch of files from the federal investigation into the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein made public on Friday includes a friendly email that was apparently sent to Epstein\u2019s accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell in late October 2002, signed \u201cLove, Melania\u201d.
 \n  
Although the email addresses of both the sender and the recipient are redacted, a second copy of the same email text also appears in another document released on Friday, which includes a reply from \u201cG. Max\u201d.
 \n  
The first email, sent on the evening of Wednesday, 23 October 2002, with the subject line \u201cHI!\u201d begins \u201cDear G!\u201d It continues:
 \n  
 \n   
How are you? Nice story about JE in NY mag. You look great on the picture.
 \n   
I know you are very busy flying all over the world. How was Palm Beach? I cannot wait to go down. Give me a call when you are back in NY. Have a great time!
 \n   
Love, Melania
 \n  
 \n  
The email was sent the week that New York magazine published a flattering profile of Jeffrey Epstein that included a photograph of Maxwell with Epstein. (The article was in the 28 October 2002 edition, but new issues of the magazine are published one week prior to the cover date.)
 \n  
That New York magazine article, published three years before police in Palm Beach first investigated Epstein for the alleged sexual abuse of a 14-year-old girl, also included quote from the future president, Donald Trump, praising his friend.
 \n  
\u201cI\u2019ve known Jeff for fifteen years. Terrific guy,\u201d Trump told reporter Landon Thomas. \u201cHe\u2019s a lot of fun to be with. It is even said that he likes beautiful women as much as I do, and many of them are on the younger side. No doubt about it \u2013 Jeffrey enjoys his social life.\u201d
 \n  
In her reply, G. Max wrote:
 \n  
 \n   
Sweet pea thanks for your message. Actually plans changed again and I am now on my way back to NY. I leave again on Fri so I still do not think I have time to see you sadly. I will try and call though.
 \n   
Keep well
 \n   
Gx
 \n  
 \n  
While the redactions in the documents mean that there is no proof that the exchange was with the future first lady, then known as Melania Knauss, Maxwell had socialized with the future Melania Trump in Palm Beach prior to the email exchange. Just over two weeks later, on 11 November 2002, they were photographed together in New York, along with Donald Trump and Naomi Campbell, at a Dolce & Gabbana event.
 \n  
Just over two months later, in January 2003, Maxwell would present Epstein with a bound volume of 50th birthday greetings from friends and associates, including a crude drawing and enigmatic message in the name of Donald Trump.

Epstein survivors outraged new documents expose names of victims 'while the men who abused us remain hidden and protected'
 \n 
 \n  
In a new statement, 20 survivors of Jeffrey Epstein\u2019s abuse expressed outrage on Friday that the partial release of documents from the federal investigation of his crimes includes \u201cnames and identifying information\u201d of victims, \u201cwhile the men who abused us remain hidden and protected\u201d.
 \n  
Here is the complete statement:
 \n  
 \n   
This latest release of Jeffrey Epstein files is being sold as transparency, but what it actually does is expose survivors. Once again, survivors are having their names and identifying information exposed, while the men who abused us remain hidden and protected. That is outrageous. As survivors, we should never be the ones named, scrutinized, and retraumatized while Epstein\u2019s enablers continue to benefit from secrecy. This is a betrayal of the very people this process is supposed to serve.
 \n   
Virginia Roberts Giuffre alone reported many abusers connected to Epstein\u2019s network, yet the public still does not have the full truth about who enabled him, who participated in his exploitation, and who has been shielded for years. Hundreds of women have come forward with additional reports like hers. The scale of this failure is staggering and indefensible.
 \n   
The Justice Department cannot claim it is finished releasing files until every legally required document is released and every abuser and enabler is fully exposed. We need to hear directly from Attorney General Pam Bondi when she appears before the House Judiciary Committee on February 11. Survivors deserve answers, and the public deserves the truth.
 \n   
This is not over. We will not stop until the truth is fully revealed and every perpetrator is finally held accountable. As we have always said, this is not about politics. We hope Democrats and Republicans will stand with survivors in continuing to demand the full release of the Epstein files.
 \n   
We look forward to hearing from Attorney General Pam Bondi on February 11.
 \n  
 \n  
The statement was signed by: Annie Farmer, Anouska de Georgiou, Ashley Rubright, AW, Danielle Bensky, Jane Doe, Jane Doe, JD, Jess Michaels, Juliette Bryant, Lara Blume McGee, Liz Stein, Marijke Chartouni, Marina Lacerda, Rachel Benavidez, Sky & Amanda Roberts, Sharlene Rochard, Teresa J Helm and Wendy Pesante.

 10.41pm GMT 
 \n 
 \n  
Elon Musk had more extensive \u2013 and more friendly \u2013 communications with the financier and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein than previously publicly known, according to documents released on Friday by the Department of Justice. Emails in the files appear to show the two cordially messaging each other on two separate occasions to make plans for Musk to visit Epstein\u2019s island.
 \n  
The documents include Musk and Epstein emailing in both 2012 and 2013 to determine when Musk should make the trip to Little St James. Neither exchanges appear to have resulted in Musk visiting the island, due to logistical issues.
 \n  
\u201cWill be in the BVI/St Bart\u2019s area over the holidays. Is there a good time to visit?\u201d Musk states on 13 December 2013.
 \n  
\u201cany day 1st - 8th . play it by ear if you want. always space for you,\u201d Epstein replies.
 \n  
Musk then sends several emails relaying his schedule, and the two settle on 2 January as a date for the visit. The email exchange ends with Epstein telling Musk that he would need to remain in New York and sending his regrets that they could not meet.
 \n  
\u201cBad news- Unfortunately , my schedule will keep me in New York . I was really looking forward to finally spending some time together with just fun as the agenda. so i am very disappointed. Hopefully we can schedule another time in the near future,\u201d Epstein wrote.
 \n  
In November 2012, Epstein sent Musk an email asking \u201chow many people will you be for the heli to island\u201d.
 \n  
\u201cProbably just Talulah and me. What day/night will be the wildest party on [y]our island?\u201d Musk replied. On 2 January 2013, Musk sent Epstein an email suggesting that the visit wouldn\u2019t take place saying: \u201cLogistics won\u2019t work this time around.\u201d
 \n  
Musk has been harshly critical of those linked to Epstein, but the newly released emails appear to contradict his own longstanding denial of any ties of his own. The Tesla CEO told Vanity Fair in 2019 that Epstein was \u201cobviously a creep\u201d and claimed that Epstein \u201ctried repeatedly to get me to visit his island. I declined.\u201d The emails between the two moguls come years after Epstein was convicted in 2008 of soliciting prostitution from a minor in Florida. Authorities later arrested Epstein in 2019 on federal sex-trafficking charges.
 \n

 9.56pm GMT 
 \n 
Justice department says Epstein files include 'untrue and sensationalist claims against President Trump'
 \n 
 \n  
In a June 2024 interview with three hosts from the Fox morning show Fox & Friends \u2013 including Pete Hegseth, who is now the US defense secretary and Rachel Campos-Duffy, whose husband is now transportation secretary \u2013 Donald Trump was asked if he would commit to \u201cdeclassify the Epstein files\u201d from the federal investigations into the late sex offender he socialized with for more than a decade.
 \n  
\u201cYeah, yeah, I would,\u201d Trump answered.
 \n  
But the version of the interview first broadcast on the show left out what Trump added immediately after that: \u201cI guess I would. I think that less so because you don\u2019t know \u2013 you don\u2019t want to affect people\u2019s lives if it\u2019s phoney stuff in there, cause there\u2019s a lot of phony stuff with that whole \u2026 world.\u201d
 \n  
On Friday, as Trump\u2019s justice department moved to comply, at least in part, with the law by releasing millions of files from the federal investigations into Epstein, it has released at least some unverified allegations against him from those files.
 \n  
One of the documents getting the most attention online is an email from 2020 that includes uncorroborated tips about Trump\u2019s own alleged involvement with Epstein\u2019s victims that were made to the FBI\u2019s National Threat Operations Center.
 \n  
The document, which was briefly inaccessible after it was posted, has been described as \u201cincriminating Trump\u201d by some critics, but the justice department provided a statement to the Guardian calling these uncorroborated tips \u201cfake\u201d.
 \n  
Here is the justice department\u2019s statement to the Guardian:
 \n  
 \n   
This production may include fake or falsely submitted images, documents or videos, as everything that was sent to the FBI by the public was included in the production that is responsive to the Act. Some of the documents contain untrue and sensationalist claims against President Trump that were submitted to the FBI right before the 2020 election. To be clear, the claims are unfounded and false, and if they have a shred of credibility, they certainly would have been weaponized against President Trump already.
 \n  
 \n  
It is impossible to verify, from the partially redacted document, if one element of the justice department statement is true. The document is a series of emails with what appear to be screenshots from another document, rounding up what someone in the FBI refers to as \u201cTrump accusers\u201d. Those emails were sent in August 2020, three months before that year\u2019s election that Trump went on to lose. But the names of the accusers, and any information about when the tips were called in to the FBI, is not included in what was made public, so we have no way of knowing when the accusations were made.
 \n  
Previous reporting has shown that at least one Epstein victim reported the sexual abuse of her 16-year-old sister by Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell to the FBI in 1996.
 \n

 9.20pm GMT 
 \n 
Obama ethics lawyer says Trump's justice department is illegally withholding files
 \n 
 \n  
Norm Eisen, a lawyer who served as special assistant to Barack Obama for ethics and government reform from 2009-2010, has released a statement on behalf of his non-partisan Democracy Defenders Fund on what he calls the Trump justice department\u2019s \u201cfailure to fully release all eligible files relating to the Epstein investigation, as required by the Epstein Files Transparency Act\u201d, through its new, partial release of documents.
 \n  
Eisen says:
 \n  
 \n   
These documents were due more than a month ago. Speaking at the Justice Department today, Todd Blanche announced that the Department had likely made its final release of documents. But while Blanche said the Department reviewed roughly six million records, it only plans to release about three million. Worse, he conceded the Department has been redacting records beyond what the law allows.
 \n   
They are trying to sell this as full compliance and the \u2018complete\u2019 Epstein record. But everything about their rollout signals the same old playbook: heavy redactions, selective disclosure, and a public-facing archive that does not reliably reflect what the government actually has.
 \n   
Again, the Department says: trust us. Again, we will not take up their insincere offer. In the hours and days ahead, we will scrutinize every page. We have litigation pending, and we are prepared to use every available legal remedy to compel full compliance and complete production, while taking every step to protect the privacy and dignity of the victims.\u201d
 \n

Here\u2019s more from the Guardian\u2019s Geraldine McKelvie on what the newly released files reveal about Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor\u2019s interactions with Jeffrey Epstein during a visit to New York City in 2010 \u2013 after the financier\u2019s conviction on child sexual abuse charges in Florida:

Documents show Epstein transferred money to husband of former UK ambassador to Washington
 \n 
 \n  
The newly released justice department documents reveal more about Jeffrey Epstein\u2019s ties to Peter Mandelson, who was London\u2019s ambassador to the United States until his sacking last year, after the extent of his ties to the disgraced financier became public.
 \n  
Here\u2019s more, from the Guardian\u2019s Emine Sinmaz:
 \n  
 \n   
Jeffrey Epstein sent thousands of pounds in bank transfers after his release from prison in 2009 to Peter Mandelson\u2019s husband, according to emails published by the US Department of Justice on Friday.
 \n   
The latest documents raise fresh questions about Epstein\u2019s relationship with Mandelson, who was sacked as the UK\u2019s ambassador to Washington when details of his support for the disgraced financier emerged in September.
 \n   
The latest data set published on Friday shows that Mandelson\u2019s husband, Reinaldo Avila da Silva, emailed Epstein on 7 September 2009, about two months after Epstein was released from prison. Epstein had served 13 months of an 18-month sentence for soliciting prostitution from a minor, for which he was registered as a sex offender. Mandelson was business secretary at the time and in a relationship with da Silva. The pair married in 2023 after 27 years together.
 \n   
Da Silva asked Epstein to fund an osteopathy course and other expenses, saying: \u201cI sent you a couple of emails last week regarding my osteo course expenses, incl fee, anatomical models, laptop if you can help me with this. I hope you received them.
 \n   
\u201cI just managed to speak to the fees office at the osteo school and confirmed that my annual fee is of \u00a33,225 ... They accept bank transfer and the details are as follows.\u201d
 \n   
Epstein responded later that day and said: \u201cI will wire your loan amount immediated\u2019y [sic].\u201d
 \n  
 \n

 \n

Here\u2019s a look back, from the Guardian\u2019s Victoria Bekiempis, on the unique federal law that mandates release of the Epstein files, and how the justice department has been criticized for not releasing them quickly enough:
 \n  
The law was clear: Donald Trump\u2019s Department of Justice was required to disclose all investigative files on Jeffrey Epstein by 19 December 2025, with rare exceptions.
 \n  
One month after this deadline mandated by Congress\u2019s Epstein Files Transparency Act, however, Trump\u2019s justice department has not complied with this law, prompting questions about when \u2013 and whether \u2013 authorities will ever release investigative documents about the late sex offender.
 \n  
Justice department attorneys said in a 5 January Manhattan court filing that they had posted approximately 12,285 to DoJ\u2019s website, equating to some 125,575 pages, under this legislation\u2019s requirements. They said in this same letter that justice department staff had identified \u201cmore than 2 million documents potentially responsive to the Act that are in various phases of review\u201d.
 \n  
That these DoJ disclosures apparently comprise a drop in the bucket \u2013 and have done little to shed light on how Epstein operated with apparent impunity for years \u2013 has roiled survivors\u2019 advocates and lawmakers. They include attorney Spencer Kuvin, who has represented dozens of Epstein\u2019s survivors.
 \n  
\u201cCongress did not create a discretionary timeline \u2013 it created a legal obligation. Every day these records remain withheld sends a message to victims that transparency is optional when powerful interests are involved,\u201d Kuvin said. \u201cFor survivors of Epstein\u2019s abuse, this delay is not procedural \u2013 it is personal.

                    "bodyText": "Emails released by the justice department on Friday show that Jeffrey Epstein joked with his brother Mark about his friendship with Woody Allen in 2012, years after he was first convicted of sex crimes but managed to find his way back into New York society. The partially redacted email exchange, in March 2012, begins with Mark Epstein, using an email address that was revealed as his in another document, asking his brother about the possibility that their parents had sex in the bath when they were children. After Jeffrey Epstein replies \u201cAghhhhhjh\u201d, Mark Epstein asks him where he is. \u201cParis with woody allen\u201d Jeffrey Epstein answers. \u201cFor les pedophile convention?\u201d Mark Epstein asks. \u201ci think pedophiles is the plural\u201d Jeffrey Epstein replies. As CBS News reported last year, previously released records show that Allen and his wife, Soon-Yi Previn, were among Epstein\u2019s most frequent social companions in the years leading up to his death. The records showed nearly 100 instances between 2014 and 2019 in which Allen and Epstein \u2013 almost always joined by Previn \u2014 were scheduled to spend time together. The files from the federal investigations into Jeffrey Epstein, the late sex offender who socialized with Donald Trump for more than a decade, include 74 documents that refer to the fact that Trump called Epstein \u201ca lot of fun to be with\u201d in a flattering 2002 New York magazine profile of the financier. \u201cI\u2019ve known Jeff for 15 years. Terrific guy,\u201d Trump told the New York writer Landon Thomas in 2002. \u201cHe\u2019s a lot of fun to be with. It is even said that he likes beautiful women as much as I do, and many of them are on the younger side. No doubt about it \u2013 Jeffrey enjoys his social life.\u201d Trump\u2019s assessment of Epstein appears in the files dozens of times, as prosecutors dug into the disgraced financier, and his accomplice, Ghislaine Maxwell. Ro Khanna and Thomas Massie, the two congressmen who wrote the Epstein Files Transparency Act, the federal law that requires the justice department to release documents related to the investigations of Jeffrey Epstein, the late sex offender, just sent a letter to Todd Blanche, the deputy attorney general, to demand a meeting to review the unredacted files. \u201cAt a recent news conference, you stated that Members of Congress may arrange to review unredacted versions of the Department\u2019s production,\u201d Khanna, a California Democrat, and Massie, a Kentucky Republican, wrote to Blanche, who was previously Donald Trump\u2019s personal lawyer. \u201cGiven ongoing reported concerns regarding the scope and consistency of redactions in the documents released to date, we respectfully request a meeting to review the unredacted records.\u201d The letter continues: In particular, we seek access to the following categories of materials: First, hundreds of thousands of pages of emails and other documents recovered from Jeffrey Epstein\u2019s email accounts during the 2018 and 2019 investigations into Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell. Second, victim interview statements from the initial Florida investigation and subsequent investigations in New York. We understand that the Department possesses FBI Form 302 reports documenting these interviews. However, the materials released to date in this category consist largely of pages that are fully redacted, providing no meaningful information for oversight or public accountability. Third, the 53-page draft indictment and the 82-page prosecution memorandum prepared during the 2007 Florida investigation. These documents are essential to understanding the government\u2019s knowledge of Epstein\u2019s criminal conduct and the circumstances surrounding the non-prosecution agreement and immunity he received. We have seen a blanket approach to redactions in some areas, while in other cases, victim names were not redacted at all. Congress cannot properly assess the Department\u2019s handling of the Epstein and Maxwell cases without access to the complete record. Accordingly, we request your assistance in arranging a secure, in-person review of these unredacted materials at the Department\u2019s earliest convenience. The new batch of files from the federal investigation into the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein made public on Friday includes a friendly email that was apparently sent to Epstein\u2019s accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell in late October 2002, signed \u201cLove, Melania\u201d. Although the email addresses of both the sender and the recipient are redacted, a second copy of the same email text also appears in another document released on Friday, which includes a reply from \u201cG. Max\u201d. The first email, sent on the evening of Wednesday, 23 October 2002, with the subject line \u201cHI!\u201d begins \u201cDear G!\u201d It continues: How are you? Nice story about JE in NY mag. You look great on the picture. I know you are very busy flying all over the world. How was Palm Beach? I cannot wait to go down. Give me a call when you are back in NY. Have a great time! Love, Melania The email was sent the week that New York magazine published a flattering profile of Jeffrey Epstein that included a photograph of Maxwell with Epstein. (The article was in the 28 October 2002 edition, but new issues of the magazine are published one week prior to the cover date.) That New York magazine article, published three years before police in Palm Beach first investigated Epstein for the alleged sexual abuse of a 14-year-old girl, also included quote from the future president, Donald Trump, praising his friend. \u201cI\u2019ve known Jeff for fifteen years. Terrific guy,\u201d Trump told reporter Landon Thomas. \u201cHe\u2019s a lot of fun to be with. It is even said that he likes beautiful women as much as I do, and many of them are on the younger side. No doubt about it \u2013 Jeffrey enjoys his social life.\u201d In her reply, G. Max wrote: Sweet pea thanks for your message. Actually plans changed again and I am now on my way back to NY. I leave again on Fri so I still do not think I have time to see you sadly. I will try and call though. Keep well Gx While the redactions in the documents mean that there is no proof that the exchange was with the future first lady, then known as Melania Knauss, Maxwell had socialized with the future Melania Trump in Palm Beach prior to the email exchange. Just over two weeks later, on 11 November 2002, they were photographed together in New York, along with Donald Trump and Naomi Campbell, at a Dolce & Gabbana event. Just over two months later, in January 2003, Maxwell would present Epstein with a bound volume of 50th birthday greetings from friends and associates, including a crude drawing and enigmatic message in the name of Donald Trump. In a new statement, 20 survivors of Jeffrey Epstein\u2019s abuse expressed outrage on Friday that the partial release of documents from the federal investigation of his crimes includes \u201cnames and identifying information\u201d of victims, \u201cwhile the men who abused us remain hidden and protected\u201d. Here is the complete statement: This latest release of Jeffrey Epstein files is being sold as transparency, but what it actually does is expose survivors. Once again, survivors are having their names and identifying information exposed, while the men who abused us remain hidden and protected. That is outrageous. As survivors, we should never be the ones named, scrutinized, and retraumatized while Epstein\u2019s enablers continue to benefit from secrecy. This is a betrayal of the very people this process is supposed to serve. Virginia Roberts Giuffre alone reported many abusers connected to Epstein\u2019s network, yet the public still does not have the full truth about who enabled him, who participated in his exploitation, and who has been shielded for years. Hundreds of women have come forward with additional reports like hers. The scale of this failure is staggering and indefensible. The Justice Department cannot claim it is finished releasing files until every legally required document is released and every abuser and enabler is fully exposed. We need to hear directly from Attorney General Pam Bondi when she appears before the House Judiciary Committee on February 11. Survivors deserve answers, and the public deserves the truth. This is not over. We will not stop until the truth is fully revealed and every perpetrator is finally held accountable. As we have always said, this is not about politics. We hope Democrats and Republicans will stand with survivors in continuing to demand the full release of the Epstein files. We look forward to hearing from Attorney General Pam Bondi on February 11. The statement was signed by: Annie Farmer, Anouska de Georgiou, Ashley Rubright, AW, Danielle Bensky, Jane Doe, Jane Doe, JD, Jess Michaels, Juliette Bryant, Lara Blume McGee, Liz Stein, Marijke Chartouni, Marina Lacerda, Rachel Benavidez, Sky & Amanda Roberts, Sharlene Rochard, Teresa J Helm and Wendy Pesante. Elon Musk had more extensive \u2013 and more friendly \u2013 communications with the financier and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein than previously publicly known, according to documents released on Friday by the Department of Justice. Emails in the files appear to show the two cordially messaging each other on two separate occasions to make plans for Musk to visit Epstein\u2019s island. The documents include Musk and Epstein emailing in both 2012 and 2013 to determine when Musk should make the trip to Little St James. Neither exchanges appear to have resulted in Musk visiting the island, due to logistical issues. \u201cWill be in the BVI/St Bart\u2019s area over the holidays. Is there a good time to visit?\u201d Musk states on 13 December 2013. \u201cany day 1st - 8th . play it by ear if you want. always space for you,\u201d Epstein replies. Musk then sends several emails relaying his schedule, and the two settle on 2 January as a date for the visit. The email exchange ends with Epstein telling Musk that he would need to remain in New York and sending his regrets that they could not meet. \u201cBad news- Unfortunately , my schedule will keep me in New York . I was really looking forward to finally spending some time together with just fun as the agenda. so i am very disappointed. Hopefully we can schedule another time in the near future,\u201d Epstein wrote. In November 2012, Epstein sent Musk an email asking \u201chow many people will you be for the heli to island\u201d. \u201cProbably just Talulah and me. What day/night will be the wildest party on [y]our island?\u201d Musk replied. On 2 January 2013, Musk sent Epstein an email suggesting that the visit wouldn\u2019t take place saying: \u201cLogistics won\u2019t work this time around.\u201d Musk has been harshly critical of those linked to Epstein, but the newly released emails appear to contradict his own longstanding denial of any ties of his own. The Tesla CEO told Vanity Fair in 2019 that Epstein was \u201cobviously a creep\u201d and claimed that Epstein \u201ctried repeatedly to get me to visit his island. I declined.\u201d The emails between the two moguls come years after Epstein was convicted in 2008 of soliciting prostitution from a minor in Florida. Authorities later arrested Epstein in 2019 on federal sex-trafficking charges. In a June 2024 interview with three hosts from the Fox morning show Fox & Friends \u2013 including Pete Hegseth, who is now the US defense secretary and Rachel Campos-Duffy, whose husband is now transportation secretary \u2013 Donald Trump was asked if he would commit to \u201cdeclassify the Epstein files\u201d from the federal investigations into the late sex offender he socialized with for more than a decade. \u201cYeah, yeah, I would,\u201d Trump answered. But the version of the interview first broadcast on the show left out what Trump added immediately after that: \u201cI guess I would. I think that less so because you don\u2019t know \u2013 you don\u2019t want to affect people\u2019s lives if it\u2019s phoney stuff in there, cause there\u2019s a lot of phony stuff with that whole \u2026 world.\u201d On Friday, as Trump\u2019s justice department moved to comply, at least in part, with the law by releasing millions of files from the federal investigations into Epstein, it has released at least some unverified allegations against him from those files. One of the documents getting the most attention online is an email from 2020 that includes uncorroborated tips about Trump\u2019s own alleged involvement with Epstein\u2019s victims that were made to the FBI\u2019s National Threat Operations Center. The document, which was briefly inaccessible after it was posted, has been described as \u201cincriminating Trump\u201d by some critics, but the justice department provided a statement to the Guardian calling these uncorroborated tips \u201cfake\u201d. Here is the justice department\u2019s statement to the Guardian: This production may include fake or falsely submitted images, documents or videos, as everything that was sent to the FBI by the public was included in the production that is responsive to the Act. Some of the documents contain untrue and sensationalist claims against President Trump that were submitted to the FBI right before the 2020 election. To be clear, the claims are unfounded and false, and if they have a shred of credibility, they certainly would have been weaponized against President Trump already. It is impossible to verify, from the partially redacted document, if one element of the justice department statement is true. The document is a series of emails with what appear to be screenshots from another document, rounding up what someone in the FBI refers to as \u201cTrump accusers\u201d. Those emails were sent in August 2020, three months before that year\u2019s election that Trump went on to lose. But the names of the accusers, and any information about when the tips were called in to the FBI, is not included in what was made public, so we have no way of knowing when the accusations were made. Previous reporting has shown that at least one Epstein victim reported the sexual abuse of her 16-year-old sister by Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell to the FBI in 1996. Norm Eisen, a lawyer who served as special assistant to Barack Obama for ethics and government reform from 2009-2010, has released a statement on behalf of his non-partisan Democracy Defenders Fund on what he calls the Trump justice department\u2019s \u201cfailure to fully release all eligible files relating to the Epstein investigation, as required by the Epstein Files Transparency Act\u201d, through its new, partial release of documents. Eisen says: These documents were due more than a month ago. Speaking at the Justice Department today, Todd Blanche announced that the Department had likely made its final release of documents. But while Blanche said the Department reviewed roughly six million records, it only plans to release about three million. Worse, he conceded the Department has been redacting records beyond what the law allows. They are trying to sell this as full compliance and the \u2018complete\u2019 Epstein record. But everything about their rollout signals the same old playbook: heavy redactions, selective disclosure, and a public-facing archive that does not reliably reflect what the government actually has. Again, the Department says: trust us. Again, we will not take up their insincere offer. In the hours and days ahead, we will scrutinize every page. We have litigation pending, and we are prepared to use every available legal remedy to compel full compliance and complete production, while taking every step to protect the privacy and dignity of the victims.\u201d Here\u2019s more from the Guardian\u2019s Geraldine McKelvie on what the newly released files reveal about Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor\u2019s interactions with Jeffrey Epstein during a visit to New York City in 2010 \u2013 after the financier\u2019s conviction on child sexual abuse charges in Florida: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor attended an intimate party with the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein months after he was released from prison, files suggest. The US justice department released another cache of documents relating to the disgraced financier on Friday. They include emails from the Hollywood publicist Peggy Siegal to several high-profile figures in relation to a \u201clast-minute casual dinner\u201d for Mountbatten-Windsor, who was in New York on an \u201cunofficial private visit\u201d in December 2010. The gathering appears to have taken place at Epstein\u2019s New York home, where Mountbatten-Windsor was staying. Mountbatten-Windsor previously said the purpose of his trip was to sever ties with Epstein, who was jailed for child sexual abuse offences in July 2009. During the visit, Mountbatten-Windsor and Epstein were pictured walking together in Central Park. The former prince said in his disastrous Newsnight interview in 2019 that he chose to meet Epstein in person to end the friendship as he felt breaking the news \u201cover the telephone was the chicken\u2019s way of doing it\u201d. Epstein killed himself in prison in 2019 as he faced fresh child sexual abuse charges. Mountbatten-Windsor has withdrawn from royal life and been stripped of his titles for his links to Epstein. In 2022, he paid a reported \u00a312m settlement to Virginia Giuffre. Giuffre, who killed herself last April, claimed she was forced to have sex with Mountbatten-Windsor after being trafficked to him by Epstein. He has always strenuously denied these allegations and made the payment without admitting liability. The newly released justice department documents reveal more about Jeffrey Epstein\u2019s ties to Peter Mandelson, who was London\u2019s ambassador to the United States until his sacking last year, after the extent of his ties to the disgraced financier became public. Here\u2019s more, from the Guardian\u2019s Emine Sinmaz: Jeffrey Epstein sent thousands of pounds in bank transfers after his release from prison in 2009 to Peter Mandelson\u2019s husband, according to emails published by the US Department of Justice on Friday. The latest documents raise fresh questions about Epstein\u2019s relationship with Mandelson, who was sacked as the UK\u2019s ambassador to Washington when details of his support for the disgraced financier emerged in September. The latest data set published on Friday shows that Mandelson\u2019s husband, Reinaldo Avila da Silva, emailed Epstein on 7 September 2009, about two months after Epstein was released from prison. Epstein had served 13 months of an 18-month sentence for soliciting prostitution from a minor, for which he was registered as a sex offender. Mandelson was business secretary at the time and in a relationship with da Silva. The pair married in 2023 after 27 years together. Da Silva asked Epstein to fund an osteopathy course and other expenses, saying: \u201cI sent you a couple of emails last week regarding my osteo course expenses, incl fee, anatomical models, laptop if you can help me with this. I hope you received them. \u201cI just managed to speak to the fees office at the osteo school and confirmed that my annual fee is of \u00a33,225 ... They accept bank transfer and the details are as follows.\u201d Epstein responded later that day and said: \u201cI will wire your loan amount immediated\u2019y [sic].\u201d Peter Mandelson said on Friday: \u201cI was wrong to believe Epstein following his conviction and to continue my association with him afterwards. I apologise unequivocally for doing so to the women and girls who suffered. \u201cI was never culpable or complicit in his crimes. Like everyone else I learned the actual truth about him after his death. \u201cBut his victims did know what he was doing, their voices were not heard and I am sorry I was among those who believed him over them.\u201d Several photos released today by the justice department show Jeffrey Epstein\u2019s cell in New York City\u2019s Metropolitan correctional center following his death in 2019. The financier\u2019s death was ruled a suicide: Also released was a shot of its exterior, following his death: The newly released files reveal the proposed guest list for a dinner Jeffrey Epstein convened in 2010 when the former prince Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was staying at his house in New York City. \u201cGeorge: do not think less of me but I am putting together a very last minute casual dinner for Prince Andrew, who is in New York on an unofficial private visit,\u201d publicist Peggy Siegal wrote to George Stephanopoulos on 1 December 2010 in an email with the subject line \u201cThursday small dinner for Prince Andrew\u201d. Stephanopoulos is a former White House communications director to Bill Clinton turned broadcast journalist. Siegal continued: The list for far...and we arc keeping this private and small... Prince Andrew, Woody Allen and Soon-Yi, Katie Couric....leffrey Epstein, where Andrew is staying. Jeffrey\u2019s house is one the largest single dwellings in New York...it\u2019s beautiful. So come to for a very interesting, fast. fun dinner Stephanopoulos replied that he could make it, but would have to leave early, prompting Siegal to reply: Totally fine. That\u2019s why we are starting at 8:00pm. So come on time and you will have private time with Andrew because he is staying at the house.... Stephanopoulos later bowed out, the emails show, saying his daughters were sick. Among the new photos released in the latest batch of Epstein files is one showing his cell following his 2019 death, which investigators determined to be a suicide. The photo shows strips of orange cloth over a railing and in a corner of a cell in the Metropolitan correctional center in New York City, where Epstein was detained while awaiting trial on sex-trafficking charges. Also included in the release is an 89-page report from New York City\u2019s chief medical examiner into his death. Ro Khanna, the Democratic congressman who was a key force in getting the Epstein Files Transparency Act signed into law, was similarly skeptical of deputy attorney general Todd Blanche\u2019s claim that the justice department had released all the files the act required them to. \u201cThe DOJ said it identified over 6 million potentially responsive pages but is releasing only about 3.5 million after review and redactions. This raises questions as to why the rest are being withheld,\u201d Khanna said in a statement. He continued: I will be reviewing closely to see if they release what I\u2019ve been pushing for: the FBI 302 victim interview statements, a draft indictment and prosecution memorandum prepared during the 2007 Florida investigation, and hundreds of thousands of emails and files from Epstein\u2019s computers. Failing to release these files only shields the powerful individuals who were involved and hurts the public\u2019s trust in our institutions. Robert Garcia, the Democratic ranking member on the House oversight committee which has taken a lead role in investigating the government\u2019s handling of Jeffrey Epstein\u2019s prosecutions, accused attorney general Pam Bondi of breaking the law after her deputy Todd Blanche indicated the department would release no further files related to the disgraced financier. \u201cDonald Trump and his Department Justice have now made it clear that they intend to withhold roughly 50% of the Epstein files, while claiming to have fully complied with the law. This is outrageous and incredibly concerning,\u201d Garcia said in a statement. \u201cThe Oversight Committee subpoena directs Pam Bondi to release all the files to the committee, while protecting survivors. They are in violation of the law.\u201d The Republican-controlled oversight committee\u2019s investigation has resulted in the release of several documents that have shed light on Epstein\u2019s relationship with powerful figures including Donald Trump: Also in this trove of files is Ghislaine Maxwell\u2019s US naturalization certificate, which lists her home address at Little St James Island, one of Epstein\u2019s two private islands in the US Virgin Islands. Asked at the press conference earlier about survivors that have \u201cexpressed frustration\u201d at the DoJ\u2019s process for releasing the files, Blanche responded: \u201cSame here.\u201d If there\u2019s frustration with quote, the entire process, same here. \u201cThe victims of Epstein have gone through unspeakable pain,\u201d he added. He said that he hopes that the release of the files has been able to \u201cbring closure\u201d to the victims. Here\u2019s a look back, from the Guardian\u2019s Victoria Bekiempis, on the unique federal law that mandates release of the Epstein files, and how the justice department has been criticized for not releasing them quickly enough: The law was clear: Donald Trump\u2019s Department of Justice was required to disclose all investigative files on Jeffrey Epstein by 19 December 2025, with rare exceptions. One month after this deadline mandated by Congress\u2019s Epstein Files Transparency Act, however, Trump\u2019s justice department has not complied with this law, prompting questions about when \u2013 and whether \u2013 authorities will ever release investigative documents about the late sex offender. Justice department attorneys said in a 5 January Manhattan court filing that they had posted approximately 12,285 to DoJ\u2019s website, equating to some 125,575 pages, under this legislation\u2019s requirements. They said in this same letter that justice department staff had identified \u201cmore than 2 million documents potentially responsive to the Act that are in various phases of review\u201d. That these DoJ disclosures apparently comprise a drop in the bucket \u2013 and have done little to shed light on how Epstein operated with apparent impunity for years \u2013 has roiled survivors\u2019 advocates and lawmakers. They include attorney Spencer Kuvin, who has represented dozens of Epstein\u2019s survivors. \u201cCongress did not create a discretionary timeline \u2013 it created a legal obligation. Every day these records remain withheld sends a message to victims that transparency is optional when powerful interests are involved,\u201d Kuvin said. \u201cFor survivors of Epstein\u2019s abuse, this delay is not procedural \u2013 it is personal. The justice department\u2019s Epstein Library now includes an age verification, asking users if they\u2019re over 18. Blanche earlier told reporters that some of the content being released includes pornography, with redactions. Among the files released by the US justice department today is a copy of Ghislaine Maxwell\u2019s police booking intake form from July 2020. It includes a picture of Maxwell in what looks like a prison orange jumpsuit, along with personal details including her full name and a redacted address in Bradford, New Hampshire. Here\u2019s a quick rundown of what Blanche said is not in the release: files that contain personally identifiable information of victims or victims\u2019 personal and medical files, and any similar files that, if disclosed, would constitute a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy any depiction of child sexual abuse material or child abuse images anything that would jeopardize an active federal investigation anything that depicts or contains images of death, physical abuse or injury files covered by various privileges, including deliberative process privilege, work product privilege, and attorney client privilege \u201cAlthough the act allows for withholding for items necessary to keep secret in the interest of national security or foreign policy, no files are being withheld or redacted on that basis,\u201d Blanche added. Blanche says he won\u2019t be commenting on criticism the DoJ has faced on its handling of the release of the files and defends its missing the congressionally set deadline. People can criticise all they want, my point was to make plain that when it comes to what we\u2019ve been doing the past two months and why, we weren\u2019t able to complete the review of over six million pages. You\u2019re talking about two Eiffel Towers of pages in 30 days in a way that made sure we complied with the act. He says the department was \u201cobviously\u201d not defying the 30-day deadline set by Congress (a reminder, that expired in December), but was complying with the need to protect victims. Blanche tells reporters: There\u2019s this built in assumption that somehow there\u2019s this hidden tranche of information of men that we know about that we\u2019re covering up or that we\u2019re choosing not to prosecute. That is not the case. I don\u2019t know whether there are men out there that abused these women. If we learn about information and evidence that that allows us to prosecute them, you better believe we will. But I don\u2019t think that the public or you all are going to uncover men within the Epstein files that abuse women. The deputy attorney general also said that no further files were due to be released. Todd Blanche told reporters: \u201cToday\u2019s release marks the end of a very comprehensive document identification and review process to ensure transparency to the American people and compliance with the act.\u201d During his press conference on Friday morning, Todd Blanche addressed redactions made by the justice department. We redacted every woman depicted in any image or video, with the exception of Miss [Ghislaine] Maxwell. We did not redact images of any man unless it was impossible to redact the woman without also redacting the man. To this end, though, and to ensure transparency, if any member of Congress wishes to review any portions of the responsive production in any unredacted form, they are welcome to make arrangements with the department to do so. The files, posted to the DoJ website, include some of the several million pages of records that officials said were withheld from an initial release of documents in December. They were disclosed under the Epstein Files Transparency Act, which was enacted after months of public and political pressure on the Trump administration. Blanche also told reporters earlier that the White House \u201chad nothing to do\u201d with the DoJ\u2019s review of the files it released today. Asked if he had updated the White House about today\u2019s announcement, Blanche replied: They had nothing to do with this review. They had no oversight over this review. They did not tell this department how to do our review, what to look for, what to redact, what to not redact. Blanche added that the White House knew he was holding today\u2019s news conference and that the DoJ was releasing the files, but \u201cthere\u2019s no oversight by the White House into the process that we\u2019ve undertaken over the past 60 days\u201d. Blanche insists that no men, including Trump, were protected in the release of the Epstein files. I can assure that we complied with the statute, we complied with the act. We did not protect President Trump. We didn\u2019t protect or not protect anybody, I think there\u2019s a hunger or a thirst for information that I do not think will be satisfied by the review of these documents. There\u2019s nothing I can do about that. Trump\u2019s direction to the DoJ was to be \u201ctransparent\u201d and \u201cthat\u2019s exactly what we did\u201d, Blanche says. Deputy attorney general Todd Blanche held a news conference at 11am ET at the Department of Justice, Washington DC. He announced that the justice department is releasing more than 3m pages from its Jeffrey Epstein files. Blanche said they include 2,000 videos and 180,000 images related to Epstein. Blanche added that the images included lots of commercial pornography and images seized from Epstein\u2019s devices. Our full report is here:",

                "id": "politics/2026/jan/30/treasurer-jim-chalmers-inflation-tax-reform-australia",
                "type": "article",
                "sectionId": "politics",
                "sectionName": "Politics",
                "webPublicationDate": "2026-01-31T02:47:27Z",
                "webTitle": "Chalmers rejects opposition claims Labor is fuelling inflation, and says he is \u2018impatient for reform\u2019",
                "webUrl": "https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/jan/30/treasurer-jim-chalmers-inflation-tax-reform-australia",
                "apiUrl": "https://content.guardianapis.com/politics/2026/jan/30/treasurer-jim-chalmers-inflation-tax-reform-australia",
                "fields": {
                    "headline": "Chalmers rejects opposition claims Labor is fuelling inflation, and says he is \u2018impatient for reform\u2019",
                    "standfirst": "
Australian treasurer \u2018open\u2019 to tax reform and says government wants to tackle  intergenerational inequity
  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast
",
                    "trailText": "Australian treasurer \u2018open\u2019 to tax reform and says the government wants to tackle intergenerational inequity",
                    "byline": "Tom McIlroy and Patrick Commins",
                    "main": "",
                    "body": "
Jim Chalmers says the May budget will help tackle inflation and strengthen the economy against shocks from Donald Trump\u2019s policies, and has pushed back on opposition claims his government is intensifying cost-of-living pain. 

Days before another expected interest rate rise from the Reserve Bank of Australia, Chalmers labelled criticism of government spending from the Liberal and National parties as hypocritical, while also saying the government was \u201copen\u201d to big ideas on tax reform and would apply a laser-focus on intergenerational inequity in Labor\u2019s second term.

\u201cThe same people who say now that the budget is the sole or primary driver of inflation weren\u2019t saying that last year when inflation was falling substantially and the bank cut rates three times,\u201d he said.
 
 
 Related: Expectations grow for interest rate hike next week after Australia\u2019s inflation jumps to 3.8%  
 
  
\u201cWe actually improved the budget in December in the update in any case, another $20bn in savings and the sort of responsibility and restraint unrecognisable to our predecessors.\u201d
 
Chalmers praised last week\u2019s landmark speech by Canada\u2019s prime minister, Mark Carney, but stopped short of endorsing Carney\u2019s call for a coalition of middle powers and said Australia would navigate a path between China, as its biggest trading partner, and the United States as a vital defence ally.
 
In a wide-ranging interview with Guardian Australia, Chalmers revealed that a new intergenerational report [IGR] would be released in the middle of the year, and was likely to include a greater-than-usual focus on geopolitics.
 
The five-yearly federal government reports are designed to project budget and economic outlooks for the next 40 years, measuring long-term policy and structural trends.
 
Sign up: AU Breaking News email
 
\u201cThe 2020s are a defining decade in terms of setting us up for the future, but also a dangerous decade, so the IGR will help paint a picture of our understandings in the 2020s about how the world will play out in the coming decade,\u201d he said.
 
He pushed back against claims his government was not acting boldly and quickly enough to lift the economy\u2019s productive capacity, saying the breadth of Labor\u2019s agenda was under-appreciated.
 
\u201cI\u2019m impatient for reform, but I\u2019m not impetuous about it,\u201d he said.
 
On the prospect of a major tax reform proposal in time for the next election, Chalmers said Labor was working on a substantial agenda already, including from last year\u2019s productivity round table and Friday\u2019s announcement of an independent review of thin capitalisation reforms. The rules are designed to prevent companies claiming excessive debt deductions to minimise the tax they pay in Australia.
 
\u201cWe take decisions collectively in our government, and any steps beyond that will be consistent with the directions that we set at the reform round table, which were around intergenerational fairness, attracting investment and making the system simpler,\u201d he said.
 
 
 Related: Mark Carney tells Davos the old world order is \u2018not coming back\u2019 as Trump heads to Switzerland 
 
  
\u201cIf there are responsible steps that we can take beyond that already very substantial agenda, and if we can afford to do that, obviously we\u2019re open to ideas. But decisions about any further tax reforms, whether it be in this May budget or subsequently, will be, as they always are, a matter for the cabinet to determine.\u201d
 
Figures on Wednesday showed inflation had jumped to 3.8% in the year to December, from 3.4% the month before, strengthening expectations of a Reserve Bank rate rise on Tuesday.
 
The return of high inflation threatens to hijack Labor\u2019s second term economic agenda in the short term, but Chalmers said he remained focused on longer-term challenges around productivity and intergenerational inequity.
 
\u201cThe government\u2019s priorities [are] dealing with this inflation challenge, turning around a couple of decades of underperforming on productivity, [and] making our economy more resilient.
 
\u201cWe\u2019re interested in building more homes for people. You know that the housing market is really one of the defining elements of this big intergenerational challenge that we have in our economy and in our society, and so those are the sorts of lenses through which we view the preparations for May.\u201d
  
 
 
Divisive politics are anathema to economic progress
 
 
  
Chalmers said Carney\u2019s speech at the World Economic Forum in Davos was a reminder decision makers in Australia should not be \u201cnostalgic\u201d about the past, especially after economic shocks including the Covid-19 pandemic and the global financial crisis.
 
\u201cThe point that Carney is making goes beyond trade policy changes out of [Washington] DC, it captures the whole shebang,\u201d he said, pointing to Russia\u2019s invasion of Ukraine, \u201ca more assertive China\u201d and Middle East conflict.
 
\u201cBut we work across the board in the service of our interests. We work with our allies, like the US, big economies like China and increasingly, middle powers like Canada.\u201d
 
Chalmers said there was an \u201cextraordinary\u201d level of interest in Australia from global investors, which he said reflected the potential for Australia to prosper despite the rupture in the global economic order.
 
\u201cWe are increasingly seen as this island of stability and opportunity in a sea of risk and uncertainty.
 
\u201cWe\u2019ve got so much of what the world needs. We\u2019ve got the stability that the world is hankering for, and that makes us more attractive. And there\u2019s economic opportunity in that for Australia, for our workers and businesses and investors, and we intend to make the most of that.\u201d
 
Carney is scheduled to address the Australian federal parliament in March.
 
Despite polls showing One Nation has a record-high primary vote of 22%, Chalmers told Guardian Australia support for rightwing parties was fracturing, pointing to the split between the Liberal party and the Nationals. 

\u201cI think they\u2019re splintering, and obviously the divisive politics of the three far-right parties in Australia risk making the intergenerational challenge worse, not better, because divisive politics are anathema to economic progress.\u201d
  ",

                "id": "world/2026/jan/31/ukraine-war-briefing-rising-us-iran-tensions-key-peace-talks-in-uae",
                "type": "article",
                "sectionId": "world",
                "sectionName": "World news",
                "webPublicationDate": "2026-01-31T02:27:30Z",
                "webTitle": "Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy fears rising US-Iran tensions will scupper key peace talks in UAE",
                "webUrl": "https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jan/31/ukraine-war-briefing-rising-us-iran-tensions-key-peace-talks-in-uae",
                "apiUrl": "https://content.guardianapis.com/world/2026/jan/31/ukraine-war-briefing-rising-us-iran-tensions-key-peace-talks-in-uae",
                "fields": {
                    "headline": "Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy fears rising US-Iran tensions will scupper key peace talks in UAE",
                    "standfirst": "
Apparent pause in Russia-Ukraine hostilities comes amid concern that peace talks set for Sunday in Abu Dhabi will be delayed. What we know on day 1,438
",
                    "trailText": "Apparent pause in Russia-Ukraine hostilities comes amid concern that peace talks set for Sunday in Abu Dhabi will be delayed. What we know on day 1,438",
                    "byline": "Guardian staff and agencies",
                    "main": "",
                    "body": "
     
  • Rising tensions over possible US strikes on Iran have injected fresh uncertainty into the plans for senior Ukrainian and Russian officials to meet in Abu Dhabi this weekend for another round of talks. \u201cThe date or the location may change,\u201d Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. \u201cFrom our point of view, something is happening in the situation between the United States and Iran, and those developments could affect the timing.\u201d
    •  
  • \u201cIt is very important for us that everyone we agreed with be present at the meeting, because everyone is expecting feedback,\u201d Zelenskyy told reporters in remarks released by his office on Friday. The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, had said on Wednesday that President Donald Trump\u2019s top envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who attended the previous round of talks, would not participate in the weekend meeting in Abu Dhabi. In Moscow, two sources told Reuters that Kirill Dmitriev, Putin\u2019s special envoy, would travel to Miami on Saturday for meetings with members of Trump\u2019s administration.
    •  
  • Ahead of the possible talks, there has been a notable reduction in attacks by Russia and Ukraine against each other as Ukraine continues to experience one of its coldest winters in decades, with many people living without electricity and heating. The Ukrainian capital is bracing for an especially cold spell from Sunday, with temperatures forecast to fall as low as -26C. Zelenskyy said he was waiting to see if Russia would observe a proposed pause in strikes on Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure, saying on Friday there was no formal ceasefire agreement between Ukraine and Russia, Pjotr Sauer writes. But Zelenskyy said Kyiv would halt such strikes if Moscow did the same. Donald Trump on Thursday claimed that Vladimir Putin had agreed to halt strikes on Ukraine\u2019s energy infrastructure for a week. The Kremlin has acknowledged the request but declined to say whether the Russian president had agreed to it. Spokesperson Dmitry Peskov indicated the measure would end on Sunday.
    •  
  • Zelenskky noted on Friday that in all regions, \u201cthere were indeed no strikes on energy facilities from Thursday night to Friday\u201d. \u201cUkraine is ready in reciprocal terms to refrain from strikes and today we did not strike at Russian energy facilities,\u201d he said.
    •  
  • Incoming Dutch prime minister Rob Jetten \u2013 whose D66 party struck a minority coalition deal to form a government this week \u2013 said he opposed the suggestion by some European Union leaders that the EU should reopen diplomatic channels with Russia so that Donald Trump could not set the tone for talks with Moscow. Jetten pledged that his new government would continue to support Kyiv and said he would not speak to Moscow because there were currently \u201cno indications\u201d Russia wanted to end the war in Ukraine. \u201cAnd as long as the aggression continues, we will continue our support for the Ukrainian people.\u201d He also said Europeans should have \u201ca much stronger debate about what can Europe do for itself,\u201d and stop looking at the US under Trump.
    •  
  • Meanwhile, Hungary\u2019s prime minister Viktor Orb\u00e1n has stepped up his opposition to Ukraine joining the EU, claiming the bloc was looking to admit the country in 2027 to help it benefit from the next seven-year financial budget. His comments come after Zelenskyy repeated his target to join the EU in 2027, despite some scepticism in the bloc about the accelerated process that would be required. Orb\u00e1n\u2019s comments will probably be seen as part of an increasingly fierce campaign ahead of this April\u2019s critical parliamentary election in Hungary, which could see him ousted after 16 years in office.
    •

                "id": "us-news/2026/jan/30/trump-administration-news-updates",
                "type": "article",

                "sectionName": "US news",
                "webPublicationDate": "2026-01-31T02:20:07Z",
                "webTitle": "Trump news at a glance: Epstein files release shows emails with Trump officials past and present",
                "webUrl": "https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jan/30/trump-administration-news-updates",
                "apiUrl": "https://content.guardianapis.com/us-news/2026/jan/30/trump-administration-news-updates",
                "fields": {
                    "headline": "Trump news at a glance: Epstein files release shows emails with Trump officials past and present",
                    "standfirst": "
Democrats question redactions and whether Trump officials are holding back more documents \u2013 key US politics stories from 30 January at a glance
",
                    "trailText": "Democrats question redactions and whether Trump officials are holding back more documents",
                    "byline": "Guardian staff",
                    "main": "",
                    "body": "
The US justice department has released more than 3m pages of documents related to its investigation into the disgraced financier and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, in a long-awaited announcement that appears to represent the bulk of the so-called Epstein files that have dogged Donald Trump politically.
 
While an analysis is still under way, the release exposes previously unknown financial ties and social connections between Epstein and prominent figures in the US and UK \u2013 including some in the president\u2019s orbit.
 
One back-and-forth email chain between Epstein and Elon Musk in 2012 appears to show the world\u2019s richest billionaire responding to the question \u201chow many people will you be for the heli[copter] to the island\u201d with \u201cwhat day/night will be the wildest party on =our island?\u201d
 
Musk, you may recall, formerly served as an unelected official in the Trump administration, running the \u201cdepartment of government efficiency\u201d (Doge).
 
Documents also revealed that Howard Lutnick, Trump\u2019s commerce secretary, planned a visit to Epstein\u2019s private island in December 2012, despite claiming last year that he and his wife had been so \u201crevolted\u201d by Epstein around 2005 that they decided to \u201cnever be in a room with that disgusting person ever again\u201d.
 
A day after the planned meeting, the emails appear to show that Epstein\u2019s assistant forwarded Lutnick a message from Epstein that read: \u201cNice seeing you.\u201d
  
US justice department releases more than 3 million new pages of Epstein files
  
A group of Epstein survivors released a statement condemning the justice department for naming victims while in some cases redacting the names of the accused.
 
The justice department also established an email inbox for victims to report redaction concerns and will allow members of Congress to view unredacted portions under confidentiality agreements. Democratic congressman Ro Khanna, who co-authored the Epstein Files Transparency Act to secure their official release, said the redactions are potentially suspicious.
 
Read the full story
 
US Senate approves deal to fund government and discuss ICE restrictions
  
In a 71-29 tally, the Senate overcame opposition from a handful of Republicans to rally behind a deal the president struck with Democrats, an unusual display of bipartisanship as tensions rise nationally over the presence of Immigration and Custom Enforcement (ICE) agents in US cities.
 
The package still needs approval by the House of Representatives, which is out of session and not scheduled to return until Monday, meaning a partial shutdown of the federal government was expected to begin when funding lapses at midnight Friday.
 
Read the full story
 
DoJ opens federal civil rights investigation into killing of Alex Pretti
  
\u201cWe\u2019re looking at everything that would shed light on that day,\u201d Todd Blanche, deputy to the attorney general, Pam Bondi, said at a press conference on Friday morning in Washington.
 
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) also said the FBI would lead the investigation into Pretti\u2019s killing.
 
Read the full story
 
Ex-CNN anchor arrested over anti-ICE protest at Minnesota church, later released
  
Don Lemon, the former CNN anchor, was released on Friday after being arrested late on Thursday on charges that he violated federal law during a protest at a church in Minnesota earlier this month.
 
Outside a federal courthouse in downtown Los Angeles after his release, Lemon vowed not to be silenced, saying: \u201cI have spent my entire career covering the news. I will not stop now.\u201d
 
Read the full story
 
Mexico president says Trump tariffs on Cuba\u2019s oil suppliers could trigger humanitarian crisis
  
Mexico\u2019s president, Claudia Sheinbaum, has warned that Donald Trump\u2019s move to slap new tariffs on countries sending oil to Cuba could trigger a humanitarian crisis on the island, which is already suffering from chronic fuel shortages and regular blackouts.
 
The US president signed an executive order on Thursday declaring a national emergency and laying the groundwork for such tariffs, ratcheting up the pressure to topple the communist government in Havana.
 
Read the full story
 
Trump says he believes Iran wants to make deal as he extols size of US \u2018armada\u2019
  
\u201cWe have a large armada, flotilla, call it whatever you want, heading toward Iran right now, even larger than what we had in Venezuela,\u201d the US president told reporters on Friday.
 
\u201cHopefully we\u2019ll make a deal. If we do make a deal, that\u2019s good. If we don\u2019t make a deal, we\u2019ll see what happens.\u201d
 
Read the full story
 
What else happened today:
  
     
  • The special agent in charge of the FBI\u2019s Atlanta field office was reportedly removed from his post after questioning the Trump administration\u2019s renewed interest in investigating the role of Fulton county, Georgia, in the 2020 election.
    •  
  • US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has taken custody of two children who attend the same Minnesota elementary school as Liam Ramos, the detained five-year-old who made headlines last week, according to school officials.
    •  
  • Thousands chanted and marched in New York on Friday to protest the Trump administration\u2019s escalating mass deportation campaign.
    •  
  • A man accused of trying to thwart authorities investigating Charlie Kirk\u2019s killing by falsely confessing to the deadly shooting faces up to 15 years in prison after pleading no contest to the allegation \u2013 and separately admitting to possessing child sexual abuse material.
    •  
  • In his first year back in office, Donald Trump has fundamentally reshaped the Environmental Protection Agency, initiating nearly 70 actions to undo rules protecting ecosystems and the climate. Here\u2019s how the rollbacks could harm our air and water \u2013 and worsen global heating.
    •  
  
Catching up? Here\u2019s what happened on 29 January 2026.

            {
                "id": "us-news/2026/jan/30/new-york-city-ice-trump-protest",
                "type": "article",
                "sectionId": "us-news",
                "sectionName": "US news",
                "webPublicationDate": "2026-01-31T01:36:42Z",
                "webTitle": "Thousands march in anti-ICE protest in New York City: \u2018If it\u2019s them today, it\u2019s us tomorrow\u2019",
                "webUrl": "https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jan/30/new-york-city-ice-trump-protest",
                "apiUrl": "https://content.guardianapis.com/us-news/2026/jan/30/new-york-city-ice-trump-protest",
                "fields": {
                    "headline": "Thousands march in anti-ICE protest in New York City: \u2018If it\u2019s them today, it\u2019s us tomorrow\u2019",
                    "standfirst": "
In nationwide day of action, people brave plunging cold temperatures to march in city and demonstrate against ICE
",
                    "trailText": "In nationwide day of action, people brave plunging cold temperatures to march in city and demonstrate against ICE",
                    "byline": "Jos\u00e9 Olivares in New York",
                    "main": "",
                    "body": "
Thousands chanted and marched in New York City on Friday to protest the Trump administration\u2019s escalating mass deportation campaign.
 
Among the protesters were young and old people, all braving plunging cold temperatures in thick coats, hats and gloves.
 
As the sun began setting, demonstrators chanted against Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), referring to that agency, the Ku Klux Klan, and fascism in the same breath.
 
\u201cAbolish ICE!\u201d and \u201cNo ICE, no KKK, no fascist USA!\u201d the crowds chanted. They also chanted, \u201cChinga la migra\u201d \u2013 which is a colloquial way to say \u201cfuck immigration enforcement\u201d in Spanish.
 
 
 Related: Anti-ICE protests being held across US as organizers urge national strike 
 
  
The demonstration in New York was part of a nationwide day of action advocating for \u201cno work, no school, no shopping\u201d to protest the Trump administration\u2019s brutal immigration crackdowns.
 
After a series of speeches at Foley Square, demonstrators began marching north through the ice-covered streets of Manhattan.
 
Brad Lander, a congressional candidate and former New York City comptroller who unsuccessfully ran for mayor, was among those demonstrating after spending days in Minneapolis, where federal agents ignited public outrage after shooting Renee Nicole Good and Alex Pretti to death on 7 January and 24 January, respectively.
 
People in Minneapolis \u201care heartbroken \u2013 and they are enraged\u201d, Lander said of the two 37-year-old US citizens\u2019 killings.
 
Lander, who in 2025 repeatedly protested at the New York City ICE office, where immigrants recently detained by the agency are held, also said: \u201cThey are organizing to protect their neighbors, and they know the eyes of the world are on them.\u201d
 
Young people and students led many of the chants on Friday.
 
John Eddy, a student from Las Vegas, came to the anti-ICE protest after refusing to attend class all day.
 
\u201cWe\u2019re students \u2013 we took the full day off of school,\u201d Eddy said. \u201cWe haven\u2019t been to any classes at all. We are out here.\u201d
 
His friend, Abdou Seye, had just arrived from Minneapolis, where he is from and where his family is based.
 
\u201cReally it\u2019s \u2018Fuck ICE,\u2019\u201d Seye said. \u201cYou have to do what you have to do.\u201d
 
Referring to Pretti and Good, he continued: \u201cThe thing is, if it\u2019s them today, it\u2019s us tomorrow, so we have to keep going. We have to keep this up.\u201d
 
Throughout the protests in Minneapolis, Seye observed how officials confronted demonstrators there aggressively. He said his mother, working behind the city hall building, was stuck there for nearly two days because of authorities\u2019 tactics.
 
Another protester, Julia Parris from Brooklyn, decided to come protest on Friday after watching the mass demonstrations across the country. She had participated in other demonstrations during the 2020 Black Lives Matter protests that spread after Minneapolis police murdered George Floyd there.
 
\u201cI am disgusted,\u201d Parris said. \u201cThere are no strong enough words to describe how I feel about this administration. We are fed up.\u201d
 
As demonstrators marched through the streets of New York City, stalling traffic, people in their cars began honking in solidarity. At one point, one man blasted music from his stereo and sat on top of his car, waving and smiling.
 
Beside Good and Pretti, immigration agents under the Trump administration\u2019s command have killed Keith Porter in Los Angeles and Silverio Villegas Gonz\u00e1lez in Illinois.
 
Friday\u2019s national protest leaders, many of them students at the University of Minnesota, are calling for federal immigration agent to leave Minneapolis after a nearly month-long operation there. The organizers say economic pressure through work stoppages and consumer boycotts is just one way to demand accountability and reform.
",
