                "webPublicationDate": "2026-01-30T18:43:01Z",
                "webTitle": "Jeffrey Epstein sent money to Mandelson\u2019s husband after prison release, emails suggest",
                "webUrl": "https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/jan/30/jeffrey-esptein-sent-money-peter-mandelson-husband-after-prison-release-emails-reveal",
                "apiUrl": "https://content.guardianapis.com/politics/2026/jan/30/jeffrey-esptein-sent-money-peter-mandelson-husband-after-prison-release-emails-reveal",
                "fields": {
                    "headline": "Jeffrey Epstein sent money to Mandelson\u2019s husband after prison release, emails suggest",
                    "standfirst": "
Child sex offender sent thousands of pounds to Reinaldo Avila da Silva, according to documents published by US justice department
",
                    "trailText": "Child sex offender sent thousands of pounds to Reinaldo Avila da Silva, according to documents published by US justice department",
                    "byline": "Emine Sinmaz",
                    "main": "",
                    "body": "
Jeffrey Epstein sent thousands of pounds in bank transfers after his release from prison in 2009 to Peter Mandelson\u2019s husband, according to emails published by the US Department of Justice on Friday.
 
The latest documents raise fresh questions about Epstein\u2019s relationship with Mandelson, who was sacked as the UK\u2019s ambassador to Washington when details of his support for the disgraced financier emerged in September.
 
The latest dataset published on Friday shows that Mandelson\u2019s husband, Reinaldo Avila da Silva, emailed Epstein on 7 September 2009, about two months after Epstein was released from prison. Epstein had served 13 months of an 18-month sentence for soliciting prostitution from a minor, for which he was registered as a sex offender. Mandelson was business secretary at the time and in a relationship with da Silva. The pair married in 2023 after 27 years together.
 
Da Silva asked Epstein to fund an osteopathy course and other expenses, saying: \u201cI sent you a couple of emails last week regarding my osteo course expenses, incl fee, anatomical models, laptop if you can help me with this. I hope you received them.
 
\u201cI just managed to speak to the fees office at the osteo school and confirmed that my annual fee is of \u00a33,225 \u2026 They accept bank transfer and the details are as follows.\u201d 
 
Epstein responded later that day and said: \u201cI will wire your loan amount immediated\u2019y [sic].\u201d 
    
The next day, Da Silva emailed Epstein again to ask if a \u00a310,000 payment included his school fees or if that amount had been transferred to the school itself. Epstein responded: \u201cincludedd\u201d [sic].
 
After da Silva sent details about his course, to which Epstein said he would \u201cwire the loan amount\u201d, Mandelson emailed Epstein saying: \u201cRemind him that to avoid a gift-tax filing it must be a loan.\u201d
 
Da Silva emailed Epstein on 17 September and said: \u201cthank you for the money which arrived in my account this morning\u201d.
 
Da Silva messaged Epstein again in April 2010 and shared his bank details, according to the Financial Times which first reported the allegations. Epstein reportedly forwarded the email to his accountant and said: \u201csend 13k dollars\u201d. He later instructed his accountant to \u201csend 2k per month to reinaldo\u201d [sic].
    
An email from Epstein to Mandelson on 19 July 2009 suggested the financier had met da Silva while serving the last few days of his prison sentence for soliciting prostitution. Epstein had served most of his sentence in a work-release programme that allowed him to leave jail during the day to go to his office, then return at night.
 
In the email Epstein said: \u201cyou didn\u2019t call me ,\u201e i spent an hour with rinaldo.. call me tomorrow.. at office.\u201d
 
Mandelson responded: \u201cI was immersed in Afghanistan \u2026 thanks for talking to Reinaldo. It did him (therefore me) a lot of good. You now see the problems. I cannot talk to him about these things at all, he won\u2019t listen. I am doing Sunday media then will call. Thanks again xxx.\u201d
 
Epstein replied: \u201cI as always am there.\u201d
 
Mandelson said on Friday: \u201cI was wrong to believe Epstein following his conviction and to continue my association with him afterwards. I apologise unequivocally for doing so to the women and girls who suffered.
 
\u201cI was never culpable or complicit in his crimes. Like everyone else I learned the actual truth about him after his death.
 
\u201cBut his victims did know what he was doing, their voices were not heard and I am sorry I was among those who believed him over them.\u201d
 
Earlier this month, Mandelson apologised for his association with Epstein. The latest batch of documents show Epstein and Mandelson were in frequent contact, often sending each other short messages about their whereabouts.
 
Emails released in November by the House oversight committee, which is conducting an inquiry into the US government\u2019s handling of the Epstein case, revealed Mandelson and Epstein were still in contact in 2016.

                "id": "sport/2026/jan/30/novak-djokovic-jannik-sinner-australian-open-semi-final-tennis",
                "type": "article",
                "sectionId": "sport",
                "sectionName": "Sport",
                "webPublicationDate": "2026-01-30T18:42:04Z",
                "webTitle": "Novak Djokovic thanks doubters for giving him strength after Sinner success",
                "webUrl": "https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/jan/30/novak-djokovic-jannik-sinner-australian-open-semi-final-tennis",
                "apiUrl": "https://content.guardianapis.com/sport/2026/jan/30/novak-djokovic-jannik-sinner-australian-open-semi-final-tennis",
                "fields": {
                    "headline": "Novak Djokovic thanks doubters for giving him strength after Sinner success",
                    "standfirst": "
  • \u2018There is a lot of experts that wanted to retire me\u2019
  • Serb won five-set epic to reach Australian Open final
",
                    "trailText": "\u2018There is a lot of experts that wanted to retire me,\u2019 said Novak Djokovic after beating Jannik Sinner in a five-set epic to reach the Australian Open final",
                    "byline": "Tumaini Carayol at Melbourne Park",
                    "main": "",
                    "body": "
Novak Djokovic thanked his doubters for helping to give him strength after he produced an incredible performance to defeat Jannik Sinner, the No 2 and two-time defending champion, 3-6, 6-3, 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 to reach the Australian Open final.
 
Djokovic, the fourth seed, will contest his 11th Australian Open final and 38th grand slam final overall on Sunday, his first losing the Wimbledon final in July 2024. At 38 years old, he is the oldest Australian Open men\u2019s finalist in history.
 
 
 Related: Djokovic shocks Sinner in late-night thriller to reach Australian Open final 
 
  
\u201cI never stopped believing in myself,\u201d he said. \u201cThere\u2019s a lot of people that doubt me. I see there is a lot of experts all of a sudden that wanted to retire me or have retired me many times the last couple of years.
 
\u201cI want to thank them all, because they gave me strength. They gave me motivation to prove them wrong, which I have tonight. For me, it\u2019s not a surprise, to be honest. I know what I\u2019m capable of.\u201d
 
It took an superlative display from the Serb to defeat Sinner, who has become one of the two dominant forces in men\u2019s tennis alongside Carlos Alcaraz. Djokovic played bold, offensive tennis, eviscerating his forehand, serving brilliantly in the important moments and matching the Italian\u2019s physicality despite being 14 years older than his rival.
 
\u201cI wouldn\u2019t dare to call it [my] finest ever [victory] but definitely the finest in the last couple of years,\u201d said Djokovic. \u201cUnder the circumstances and semis against Sinner, who has been playing best tennis of his life in the last couple of years, particularly here \u2026 the two-time defending champion, [it] doesn\u2019t get better than this.
 
\u201cHonestly, when I started my preparations for the new season and kind of set the goals, it\u2019s no secret that grand slams are where I want to play my best tennis. But it becomes, I guess, more difficult for me to motivate myself, and I ask myself questions. \u2018OK, what is it that I\u2019m looking for from myself?\u2019 I was imagining playing against Jannik and Carlos [Alcaraz] at the final stages of grand slams this year and battling it out and really giving it all that I have.
 
\u201cSo, very fortunate to already get it in the first slam of the year. So, yeah, big win. Very proud. Very happy. Very relieved, as well, because it was physically very demanding and gruelling.\u201d
 
Djokovic will next face Alcaraz, the No 1, after the Spaniard survived his own five-set epic against Alexander Zverev, the third seed: \u201cI know I have to come back in less than a couple of days and fight the No 1 in the world,\u201d said Djokovic. \u201cI just hope that I\u2019ll have enough gas to stay toe to toe with him. That\u2019s my desire, then let the gods decide the winner.\u201d

            {
                "id": "football/2026/jan/30/sheffield-wednesday-takeover-efl-source-of-funding-gambling",
                "type": "article",
                "sectionId": "football",
                "sectionName": "Football",
                "webPublicationDate": "2026-01-30T18:38:28Z",
                "webTitle": "Sheffield Wednesday takeover in limbo while EFL checks source of bidders\u2019 funding",
                "webUrl": "https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jan/30/sheffield-wednesday-takeover-efl-source-of-funding-gambling",
                "apiUrl": "https://content.guardianapis.com/football/2026/jan/30/sheffield-wednesday-takeover-efl-source-of-funding-gambling",
                "fields": {
                    "headline": "Sheffield Wednesday takeover in limbo while EFL checks source of bidders\u2019 funding",
                    "standfirst": "
  • EFL examining if funds mostly from gambling proceeds 
  • Bidders\u2019 advisers say money is from investments
",
                    "trailText": "The EFL is taking its time assessing the prospective buyout of Sheffield Wednesday to establish whether the purchase would be largely funded by the proceeds of gambling and crypto-gambling operations",
                    "byline": "Matt Hughes",
                    "main": "",
                    "body": "
The English Football League is taking its time assessing the prospective buyout of Sheffield Wednesday to establish whether the purchase would be largely funded by the proceeds of gambling and crypto-gambling operations.
 
A consortium was given preferred bidder status by Wednesday\u2019s administrators on Christmas Eve, with the funding coming from two of its members, the professional poker player James Bord and the crypto-gambling casino owner Felix Roemer. The EFL is assessing whether the bidders comply with the requirements of its owners\u2019 and directors\u2019 test (ODT).
 
At the end of the season those assessments are being taken over by the Independent Football Regulator and it would pick up the Wednesday case if it has not been completed. The regulator also has the authority to assess incumbent owners, and has powers of investigation, sanction and enforcement more draconian than those of the EFL.
 
The Bord/Roemer consortium has paid a multimillion-pound deposit to secure exclusive negotiating rights to buy Wednesday, and has provided evidence to the administrators, Begbies Traynor, that it has the funding to complete the proposed \u00a330m-plus purchase and three years of operating costs.
 
The sources of that funding are being analysed by the EFL, and the buyers\u2019 involvement in gambling could complicate the takeover, with sources indicating due diligence is in its early stages. An EFL spokesperson said the ODT process was ongoing.
 
Other clubs owned by gambling companies, notably Tony Bloom\u2019s Brighton and Matthew Benham\u2019s Brentford, have dispensation from the Football Association, which banned football betting for all participants in 2014. As part of that agreement Bloom and Benham allow the accounts of their betting consultancies, Starlizard and Smartodds respectively, to be independently audited on behalf of the FA to ensure they are not betting on football.
 
Bord and Roemer would have to sign a similar undertaking, although it is unclear whether the FA would grant them dispensation. Bloom and Benham were club owners when the rules were introduced. The FA is understood to be liaising with the EFL.
 
There is no public record of Bord\u2019s wealth beyond reported career poker winnings of about \u00a33m. The 44-year-old has worked for the data-driven betting businesses of Bloom and Benham, and multiple sources in the industry have described him as a successful gambler.
    
Bord\u2019s and Roemer\u2019s advisers said that the Wednesday bid was being privately funded, with the pair having made money through investments in technology and analytics, but declined to go into more details.
 
Roemer\u2019s funding appears more clearcut through his ownership of crypto-gambling casino and sports betting site, Gamdom, an offshore operation registered in the Indian Ocean Comoros Islands.
 
Bord also owns the Scottish Championship club Dunfermline with a fellow poker player, Evan Sofa, and has stakes in the Spanish club C\u00f3rdoba and the Bulgarian side Septemvri Sofia with other investors.
 
Bord\u2019s other publicly known vehicle, Short Circuit Science, a data and analytics company, appears to be based offshore beacuse it is not registered in the UK or US. There are no public details of its staffing levels or business operations. Short Circuit had a contract with Sheffield United to advise on player recruitment last year until it emerged that Bord was bidding for Wednesday.
 
Bord and Roemer beat off competition from six other bidders, including the former Newcastle owner Mike Ashley, to agree a deal to buy Wednesday after the club entered administration last October.
 
Begbies Traynor is understood to retain confidence in its preferred bidder, but is aware of the ODT process make take considerable time, which led them to sell several players this month to ensure the club have sufficient cashflow to finish the season. The club captain Barry Bannan left for Millwall and Chelsea agreed to pay \u00a3500,000 for the 17-year-old defender Yisa Alao.
 
Clive Betts, Labour MP for Sheffield South East, urged the EFL to run a rigorous process despite his desire for a sale to be completed.
 
\u201cThe source of funding has to be a concern, given the inherent volatility of those industries,\u201d Betts said. \u201cEven if the EFL approves the takeover, what level of sustainability is there? These are issues that need to be addressed. I\u2019m sure the regulator will be taking a close look, as even if they aren\u2019t running the ODT they could inherit these owners. This is a massive test for the regulator. Given the nature of the bidders they will want to ensure there\u2019s a thorough process, and it could take a long time.\u201d
",

Clive Betts, Labour MP for Sheffield South East, urged the EFL to run a rigorous process despite his desire for a sale to be completed. \u201cThe source of funding has to be a concern, given the inherent volatility of those industries,\u201d Betts said. \u201cEven if the EFL approves the takeover, what level of sustainability is there? These are issues that need to be addressed. I\u2019m sure the regulator will be taking a close look, as even if they aren\u2019t running the ODT they could inherit these owners. This is a massive test for the regulator. Given the nature of the bidders they will want to ensure there\u2019s a thorough process, and it could take a long time.\u201d",

                "id": "us-news/2026/jan/30/donald-trump-iran-end-nuclear-programme-killing-protesters-face-us-military",
                "type": "article",
                "sectionId": "world",
                "sectionName": "World news",
                "webPublicationDate": "2026-01-30T18:38:13Z",
                "webTitle": "Trump says he believes Iran wants to make deal as he extols size of US \u2018armada\u2019",
                "webUrl": "https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jan/30/donald-trump-iran-end-nuclear-programme-killing-protesters-face-us-military",
                "apiUrl": "https://content.guardianapis.com/us-news/2026/jan/30/donald-trump-iran-end-nuclear-programme-killing-protesters-face-us-military",
                "fields": {
                    "headline": "Trump says he believes Iran wants to make deal as he extols size of US \u2018armada\u2019",
                    "standfirst": "
US president declines to say whether he plans Venezuela-like operation, after Tehran signalled it was ready for talks
  • Killing Khamenei? Hitting military sites? It is unclear what a US attack on Iran would achieve
",
                    "trailText": "US president declines to say whether he plans Venezuela-like operation, after Tehran signalled it was ready for talks",
                    "byline": "Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor",
                    "main": "",
                    "body": "
Donald Trump has said he believes Tehran wants to make a deal to head off a regional conflict, as he claimed the US \u201carmada\u201d near Iran was bigger than the task force deployed to topple Venezuela\u2019s leader.
 
\u201cWe have a large armada, flotilla, call it whatever you want, heading toward Iran right now, even larger than what we had in Venezuela,\u201d the US president told reporters on Friday.
 
\u201cHopefully we\u2019ll make a deal. If we do make a deal, that\u2019s good. If we don\u2019t make a deal, we\u2019ll see what happens.\u201d
 
He declined to say whether he planned a repeat of the military operation in Venezuela in which US forces captured and renditioned the president, Nicol\u00e1s Maduro.
 
\u201cI don\u2019t want to talk about anything having to do with what I\u2019m doing militarily,\u201d he said.
 
His comments came after Iran\u2019s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi said Tehran was ready to negotiate with the US, but only if talks were not under duress and did not extend to Iran\u2019s missile programme.
 
After meetings with Turkish diplomats, Araghchi said Iran was \u201cready to begin negotiations if they take place on an equal footing, based on mutual interests and mutual respect\u201d. He said there were no immediate plans to meet US officials, adding: \u201cI want to state firmly that Iran\u2019s defensive and missile capabilities will never be subject to negotiation.\u201d
 
Araghchi said: \u201cThe Islamic Republic of Iran, just as it is ready for negotiations, is also ready for war.\u201d
 
Trump said on Thursday he hoped to avoid military action, even as the US deployed another warship to the Middle East, joining the USS Abraham Lincoln and several guided-missile destroyers.
    
But his precise objectives remain unclear. Speaking at the premiere of the documentary Melania, the US president told reporters Iran had to do \u201ctwo things\u201d to avoid military action. \u201cNumber one, no nuclear. And number two, stop killing protesters,\u201d saying that \u201cthey are killing them by the thousands\u201d.
 
He added: \u201cWe have a lot of very big, very powerful ships sailing to Iran right now, and it would be great if we didn\u2019t have to use them.\u201d
 
Iran has blamed the US and Israel for the protests that erupted in late December over economic grievances, and were brutally suppressed. Activist groups estimate as many as 30,000 people were killed in the ensuing crackdown.
 
 
 Related: \u2018Deeply ideological\u2019: the rationale behind Iran\u2019s insistence on uranium enrichment 
 
  
The Turkish foreign minister, Hakan Fidan, said the resumption of talks between Tehran and Washington over Iran\u2019s nuclear programme was \u201cvital for reducing regional tensions\u201d. Speaking alongside Araghchi, he claimed Israel was pushing for the US to attack Iran, and urged Washington to \u201cact with common sense and not allow this to happen\u201d.
 
In a call with Iran\u2019s president, Masoud Pezeshkian, Turkey\u2019s president, Recep Tayyip Erdo\u011fan, said he was willing to act as a mediator between Iran and the US. 
 
From Iran\u2019s perspective, the US is piling ever more demands on Tehran that if all were implemented would spell the end of its sovereignty.
 
Trump\u2019s special envoy Steve Witkoff has called for an end to Iran\u2019s nuclear enrichment programme, the transfer of its existing stock of highly enriched uranium out of the country, limits on Iran\u2019s missile programme and an end to support for proxy groups in countries such as Lebanon, Iraq and Yemen.
 
Araghchi held separate phone calls with his counterparts from Qatar, Egypt, the United Arab Emirates, Oman and Turkey. All the Arab states have insisted their air ground facilities cannot be used by the US to attack Iran.
 
In Turkey, Araghchi criticised Thursday\u2019s decision by the EU, likely to be followed by the UK, to proscribe the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organisation.
 
He said: \u201cThe truth is that Europe is a declining continent and has lost its role on the international level and is losing it more and more every day, and it is surprising that they themselves are fuelling this process. This shows that Europe has neither a correct understanding of the international situation, nor a correct understanding of the conditions in our region, nor a correct understanding of its own interests. The decision they made was a major strategic mistake.\u201d
 
Araghchi did not spell out what reprisals were being considered, but the UK Foreign Office has always worried such a move would lead Iran to break off diplomatic relations. But Ali Larijani, the secretary of Iran\u2019s national security council, said in future Tehran would treat the armies of Europe as terrorists.
 
The Iranian supreme leader\u2019s representative in the IRGC said the European action would have serious consequences for the EU.
 
On Friday, the US followed the EU in imposing sanctions against Iran\u2019s interior minister, accusing Eskandar Momeni of repressing the nationwide protests. The sanctions come as anger grows inside Iran that the supposedly reformist government allowed such large-scale killings.
 
In a statement, the Reform Front, a reformist umbrella body, called for \u201can independent fact-finding committee to investigate this unprecedented disaster and present a transparent and candid report to the Iranian nation\u201d.
 
It also called on the judiciary to refrain from \u201chasty rulings\u201d against detainees, and said bereaved families must be allowed to freely mourn protesters who were killed in the crackdown.

                "id": "sport/live/2026/jan/30/sri-lanka-v-england-first-mens-cricket-t20-international-live",
                "type": "liveblog",
                "sectionId": "sport",
                "sectionName": "Sport",
                "webPublicationDate": "2026-01-30T18:32:07Z",
                "webTitle": "Sri Lanka v England: Sam Curran takes hat-trick in first men\u2019s T20 international \u2013 as it happened",
                "webUrl": "https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2026/jan/30/sri-lanka-v-england-first-mens-cricket-t20-international-live",
                "apiUrl": "https://content.guardianapis.com/sport/live/2026/jan/30/sri-lanka-v-england-first-mens-cricket-t20-international-live",
                "fields": {
                    "headline": "Sri Lanka v England: Sam Curran takes hat-trick in first men\u2019s T20 international \u2013 as it happened",
                    "standfirst": "
England win a rain-interrupted match in Kandy to lead the three match series 1-0
",
                    "trailText": "England win a rain-interrupted match in Kandy to lead the three match series 1-0",
                    "byline": "James Wallace",
                    "main": "",
                    "body": "
 
 6.32pm GMT 
    
  
Ah, I was hanging on for the post match presentations but it seems they have been pulled. Time for me to skedaddle then, thanks for your company. Taha\u2019s match report will be along very soon and do join us on Sunday for match number two. 
 
The weekend has landed. Goodbye! 
 
   
 
 
 6.08pm GMT 
   
England win by 11 runs on DLS
  
  
Handshakes all round, a strange and drawn out match comes to a close. England take a 1-0 lead in the series. Adil Rashid starred with the ball, taking 3-19 before Sam Curran popped up to take a hat-trick at the end of Sri Lanka\u2019s innings. A total of 133 was never going to be enough for the home side and so it proved.
 
We\u2019ll have some reaction from the ground very soon.
   
   
Updated at 6.38pm GMT
  
 
 
 6.00pm GMT 
   
Rain Stops Play!
  
  
Oh, the rain has returned and seemingly caught everyone out. The players are going off with England eleven runs ahead on DLS. That could well be it for the action today. 
 
   
Updated at 6.13pm GMT
  
 
 
 5.58pm GMT 
   
WICKET! Phil Salt c Wellalage b Shanaka 46 (England 123-4)
  
  
Salt holes out to long on before he can chalk up what would have been a very strange half century.
   
   
Updated at 6.39pm GMT
  
 
 
 5.53pm GMT 
    
  
14th over: England 120-3 (Salt 46, Brook 12) Brook is dropped by Nissanka at deep cover! A dolly Miss Molly. Salt then throws himself into the wound with a clobbered off side four off the next ball. England need 14 more from 18 balls to go 1-0 up in the three match series. 
 
   
 
 
 5.49pm GMT 
    
  
13th over: England 115-3 (Salt 42, Brook 11) Brooky cloths a reverse off Hasaranga but somehow manages to get it to trickle away for four runs. Twenty needed for England, eyes down for a red inker. Not. 
 
   
 
 
 5.47pm GMT 
    
  
12th over: England 105-3 (Salt 38, Brook 5) Phil Salt\u2019s ten over boundary drought is lifted with a step across his stumps and a flick over the ropes off Theekshana. 
 
   
 
 
 5.44pm GMT 
    
  
11th over: England 97-3 (Salt 31, Brook 4) Hasaranga whips through a cheap and quick over. Just four runs off it, its all about wickets from here, namely can Sri Lanka take seven of \u2018em. 
 
   
 
 
 5.37pm GMT 
    
  
10th over: England 93-3 (Salt 28, Brook 3) Brook is off the mark with a scampered two past point. A top edge ploops over third for a single. England need a run a ball \u2013 42 off 42. 
 
   
 
 
 5.32pm GMT 
   
WICKET! Tom Banton c Asalanka b Pathirana 29 (England 87-3)
  
  
The home side needed that. Banton is caught at cover by Asalanka, a fine grab with two hands as the ball was middle sweetly. Harry Brook arrives in the middle.
   
   
Updated at 5.37pm GMT
  
 
 
 5.25pm GMT 
    
  
9th over: England 86-2 (Salt 26, Banton 29) Banton is doing his World Cup chances no harm at all with this sprightly cameo, he trots down and lofts Theekshana for four. England take nine off the over, Sri Lanka need wickets pronto. 
 
   
 
 
 5.24pm GMT 
    
  
8th over: England 77-2 (Salt 23, Banton 23) Salt clips a single, he\u2019s slowed right down since that rapid start, just nine off the next 13 deliveries. Banton gets on with it instead \u2013 the Somerset man reverses Hasaranga for four and then does the same for a SIX! The bowler tries a googly but Banton reads it and slaps it over midwicket for SIX more! 17 runs off the over, England need just 58 more. 
 
   
 
 
 5.17pm GMT 
    
  
7th over: England 60-2 (Salt 22, Banton 7) Banton gets a meaty outside edge off Shanaka and it runs away for four through the vacant deep third. Sri Lanka are coming back into the contest though with some tighter bowling, pace off and stump to stump. Add a couple of wickets to the score\u2026
 
   
 
 
 5.15pm GMT 
    
  
6th over: England 53-2 (Salt 20, Banton 2) Drop! Big Drop! Phil Salt picks out Mishara on the square leg boundary but the catch plops in and straight back out again. That\u2019s a huge miss. Five off the over but Hasaranga is spewing about the catch still at the end of the over, as well he might. 
 
   
 
 
 5.13pm GMT 
   
WICKET! Jacob Bethell c Shanaka b Malinga 9 (England 48-2)
  
  
Bethell flatters to deceive in his short innings, nonchalantly flicking Malinga over midwicket for four but perishing meekly off the final ball with a plink to short cover.
 
Tom Banton is the new man, a decent innings here will keep his name in the hunt for selection for the World Cup, Ben Duckett is resting in this series after a torrid Ashes but his name is thought to be the one inked in the XI.
 
5th over: England 48-2 (Salt 14, Banton 0)
   
   
Updated at 5.38pm GMT
  
 
 
 5.04pm GMT 
    
  
4th over: England 41-1 (Salt 14, Bethell 5) Bethell glides a four through point with oodles of time off Pathirana. The bowler responds with a searing 90mph yorker that Bethell does well to dig out. Sri Lanka seem convinced that it was pad first and send it upstairs\u2026 nope \u2013 he more or less middled it. A decent over though, just the one four off it as Bethell can\u2019t beat the infield. 
 
   
 
 
 5.01pm GMT 
    
  
3rd over: England 37-1 (Salt 14, Bethell 1) Jacob Bethell is the new batter, be still my beating heart. He clips a single off the last ball of the over to keep the strike. This could be fun. 
 
   
 
 
 4.59pm GMT 
   
WICKET! Jos Buttler b Malinga 17 (England 36-1)
  
  
Buttler hits four fours in a row off Eshan Malinga but is then completely foxed by a slower ball, stumps knocked back and he has to go after looking a million dollars.
   
   
Updated at 5.39pm GMT
  
 
 
 4.57pm GMT 
    
  
2nd over: England 20-0 (Salt 14, Buttler 1) Matheesha Pathirana shares the new ball, he beats Buttler first up with his zippy medium pace. A full toss goes unpunished as Buttler looks to the square leg umpire and implores for a no ball to be called. It isn\u2019t but England get four leg byes off the next to keep them ticking. 
 
   
 
 
 4.46pm GMT 
    
  
1st over: England 14-0 (Salt 14, Buttler 0) Theekshana drops short with his first ball and is flat batted for SIX by Salt. Bosh. Salt crashes a full ball through the covers for four and then follows up with a clip off his pads for another. Three boundaries in a row to start the chase for England. Three dots follow but England are in a hurry. 
 
   
 
 
 4.43pm GMT 
    
  
Righto, Phil Salt and Jos Buttler are out in the middle. Maheesh Theekshana will start with the ball for Sri Lanka, play! 
 
   
 
 
 4.35pm GMT 
   
Sri Lanka bowled out for 133
  
  
Overton rips out Hasaranga\u2019s middle dolly and that is categorcially that. The home side bundled out inside their 17 overs after a really strong start. England\u2019s spinners did the damage in the middle overs and then Sam Carran popped up to take a hat-trick (after taking some tap). 
 
England will need about 8 runs an over, I dare say they will try and get it quicker than that. Back soon for the chase! 
 
   
 
 
 4.32pm GMT 
    
  
16th over: Sri Lanka 129-9 (Hasaranga 10) Just the four runs and THREE WICKETS in the over. One more to go, in more ways than one\u2026
 
   
 
 
 4.31pm GMT 
   
Sam Curran takes a hat-trick!
  
  
Matheesha Pathirana is bowled neck and crop and Curran wheels away with arms outstretched! A HAT-TRICK! After being flogged around the park in his first couple of overs. Cricket! Bloody \u2018ell! 
 
   
 
 
 4.29pm GMT 
   
WICKET! Maheesh Theekshana c Overton b Curran 0 (Sri Lanka 129-8)
  
  
Two in two for Curran, he\u2019s on a hat-trick! 
 
   
 
 
 4.28pm GMT 
   
WICKET! Dasun Shanaka c Brook b Curran 20 (Sri Lanka 129-7)
  
  
Sam Curran has had a bad day but turns his fortunes around in his third over\u2026
 
   
 
 
 4.26pm GMT 
    
  
15th over: Sri Lanka 125-6 (Shanaka 18, Hasaranga 9) Archer back into the attack and his first ball is too straight, too full and clipped away for a SIX by Shanaka! Archer winces but comes back strong, just three singles follow in the over. Two overs to go, what can Sri Lanka muster? 
 
   
 
 
 4.23pm GMT 
    
  
14th over: Sri Lanka 116-6 (Shanaka 10, Hasaranga 8) Overton returns, drops short and is flogged away by Hasaranga. 
 
   
 
 
 4.16pm GMT 
    
  
13th over: Sri Lanka 110-6 (Shanaka 9, Hasaranga 3) Shot! A a much needed swipe for SIX by Shanaka. Dawson closes out with 2-31 from his four. England\u2019s spinners have done the damage in Kandy. 
 
   
 
 
 4.14pm GMT 
    
  
12th over: Sri Lanka 100-6 (Shanaka 1, Hasaranga 1) The hundred comes up for Sri Lanka but at 76-2 they were flying only to fall in a heap. Adil Rashid finishes with 3-19 from his four overs. Masterful. 
 
   
 
 
 4.12pm GMT 
   
WICKET! Dhananjaya de Silva c Curran b Rashid 11 (98-6)
  
  
Another one gone! Five wickets in five consecutive overs for England. Rashid bamboozled Dhananjaya with a couple of googlies and the shot to break the shackles is pouched by Curran in the deep. Implosion! 
 
   
 
 
 4.10pm GMT 
    
  
11th over: Sri Lanka 98-5 (de Silva 11, Shanaka 0) Dawson has 2-31 from his three overs, superb spin bowling. 
 
   
 
 
 4.07pm GMT 
   
WICKET! Janith Liyanage lbw b Dawson 1 (Sri Lanka 98-5)
  
  
England get one overturned on review. Dawson and Buttler were confident that Liyanage was pinned in front and no bat was involved, the replays confirm it and the batter is on his way. Sri Lanka capitulating a little in Kandy.
   
   
Updated at 4.25pm GMT
  
 
 
 4.05pm GMT 
    
  
10th over: Sri Lanka 91-4 (de Silva 2, Liyanage 1) Ten overs done and England have pegged the home side back after that rapid start. 
 
   
 
 
 4.03pm GMT 
   
WICKET! Kusal Mendis c Overton b Rashid 37 (Sri Lanka 89-4)
  
  
Rashid gets the key wicket of Kusal Mendis! A flighted leggie grips the surface and Mendis gets a big leading edge down to long on where Overton takes it in his sizeable yeoman hands.
   
   
Updated at 4.09pm GMT
  
 
 
 4.01pm GMT 
    
  
9th over: Sri Lanka 83-3 (Mendis 30, de Silva 2) Dawson fires it in full and gets out of the over cheaply, just four runs and the wicket off it. 
 
   
 
 
 3.51pm GMT 
   
WICKET! Charith Asalanka c Bethell b Dawson 2 (Sri Lanka 79-3)
  
  
Asalanka tries the big slog sweep but doesn\u2019t get enough of it, Jacob Bethell scampers round the boundary edge and takes a fine catch on the dive. England chipping their way back into the contest.
   
   
Updated at 4.21pm GMT
  
 
 
 3.50pm GMT 
    
  
8th over: Sri Lanka 79-2 (Mendis 30, Asalanka 2) Charith Asalanka is the new batter. Mishara is still out there and looking dangerous. Rashid gets out of his over for the cost of just four runs and he pocketed the all important wicket too. 
 
   
 
 
 3.47pm GMT 
   
WICKET! Pathum Nissanka c Buttler b Rashid 23 (Sri Lanka 75-2)
  
  
England needed a wicket and their main man delivers. Rashid tosses one above the eyes and Nissanka goes for a big moose across the line, he miscues and Buttler does the rest. England gather in the middle and take a few deep breaths, they were on the ropes there.
   
   
Updated at 4.21pm GMT
  
 
 
 3.45pm GMT 
    
  
7th over: Sri Lanka 75-1 (Nissanka 23, Mendis 29) Sam Curran returns and starts with some dross first up, slinging a full ball onto the pads with fine leg up in the circle, easy pickings for Kusal Mendis. Mendis then clears the front leg and swipes Curran away through midwicket for four more. SIX! Curran goes to a short ball but Mendis is onto it like a seagull on a saveloy \u2013 smashing it away over the leg side and into the crowd. Trying times for Curran\u2026 SIX MORE! Curran tries a slower ball but Mendis is ready and waiting, depositing down the ground for another big one. Twenty runs off the over \u2013 Sam Curran has 0-35 from his two. Have a breather, son. 
 
   
 
 
 3.40pm GMT 
    
  
6th over: Sri Lanka 55-1 (Nissanka 23, Mendis 9) Adil Rashid introduced with Harry Brook needing his main man to take some wickets and stem the flow. After one ball from Rashid the truncated PowerPlay is complete. Nissanka and Mendis can only deal in singles, five off the over. 
 
   
 
 
 3.38pm GMT 
    
  
5th over: Sri Lanka 50-1 (Nissanka 21, Mendis 6) Dawson into the attack, there\u2019s plenty of head scratching out in the middle as the ball appears to clip the stumps when Nissanka misses a sweep shot but the bails stay on and the ball dribbles away for four byes! Someone\u2019s UHU\u2019d the bails Guv! Nissanka is looking imperious, he makes room to cut Dawson for four and then ends the over with wonderful lofted SIX over mid-off. 
 
Ffity up for Sri Lanka \u2013 they are going at ten an over. Even I can do that maths. 
 
   
 
 
 3.34pm GMT 
    
  
4th over: Sri Lanka 36-1 (Nissanka 11, Mendis 6) Nissanka attempts a paddle sweet to Archer which I\u2019m not sure is the wisest move. He misses the ball and is smashed on the pad, Archer pleads with the umpire who says not out and Harry Brook decides against sending it upstairs, wisely as it hit Nissanka outside the line. Nissanka is a joy to watch though, he trots down and lofts Archer over cover for four. A single brings Mendis on strike, he rocks back and unleashes a cut past backward point for four more. Decent start from the home side. 
 
   
 
 
 3.29pm GMT 
    
  
3rd over: Sri Lanka 25-1 ( Mishara 10, Nissanka 6) Kusal Mendis is the new batter, Overton keeps him honest with four dots. Seven runs and the wicket off the over. 
 
   
 
 
 3.28pm GMT 
   
WICKET! Kamil Mishara c Dawson b Overton 16 (Sri Lanka 24-1)
  
  
Jamie Overton replaces Curran and is immediately mullered into the stands over long-on by Mishara. That was some strike. Gone! Mishar tries to repeat the stroke but hits it straight up up and up. Liam Dawson takes a simple catch\u2026 did I mention how safe his hands were? England get their first.
     
   
Updated at 4.23pm GMT
  
 
 
 3.25pm GMT 
    
  
2nd over: Sri Lanka 18-0 ( Mishara 10, Nissanka 6) Jofra Archer starts from t\u2019other end. He skims one past the outside edge of Mishara\u2019s bat and looks in fine fettle in his first few balls. DROP! Archer shows his frustration as Liam Dawson shells a chance at midwicket, Mishara given a life. Dawson was almost at full stretch but got there with his left hand and perhaps could have taken it he\u2019d gone with both. Just two off the over but a missed opportunity for England. I don\u2019t want to do Dawson down, but I recall seeing him drop quite a few catches in an England shirt now? Harsh but fair? 
 
   
 
 
 3.19pm GMT 
    
  
1st over: Sri Lanka 16-0 ( Mishara 9, Nissanka 5) The sky is bruised and so are Sam Curran\u2019s figures after just one over, the wee man is flogged for 16 runs off his first including three fours from over pitched deliveries that are given the treatment. Nissanka plays the pick of them with a languid cover drive that threads the field but Mishara didn\u2019t miss out either, picking off two boundaries through the off side with sweet timing. 
 
   
 
 
 3.12pm GMT 
    
  
Sam Curran is going to start with the new ball for England. Let\u2019s play!

 3.11pm GMT 
    
  
Taha chirps up from the ground and says he doesn\u2019t think there will be any more rain. Wahey.

 2.59pm GMT 
   
England win the toss and will bowl first
  
  
Harry Brook calls the coin correctly at a soggy looking Pallekele, England choose to chase. No brainer. 
 
   
 
 
 2.41pm GMT 
   
Match reduced to 17 overs per side

 Related: Jofra Archer catapulted into England T20 team a week before World Cup 
 
 
   
 
 
 12.57pm GMT 
   
Preamble
  
  
Hello and welcome to the first of three T20 Internationals between Sri Lanka and England from Kandy. After pulling off a series win in the longer stuff Harry Brook and his men are now getting down to brass tacks with the shorter format. 
 
The T20 World Cup starts in a little over a week and these matches are the final tune up, after a disastrous Ashes campaign it is fair to say that higher level jobs are in the spotlight and immediate futures will likely hinge on how England perform in the tournament. 
 
Some good news \u2013 Jofra Archer is back ahead of schedule after pulling his side in Australia, he wasn\u2019t initially named in the squad to play these matches but his early return is a boon for Harry Brook. 
 
Play will begin at 1.30pm GMT all being well, there are reports of some inclement weather in Kandy at the moment, whether the players are perched on the ground in the pouring rain, trying to make themselves a sail\u2026 remains to be seen. 
 
I\u2019ll be here OBOing for ya.

After one ball from Rashid the truncated PowerPlay is complete. Nissanka and Mendis can only deal in singles, five off the over. 5th over: Sri Lanka 50-1 (Nissanka 21, Mendis 6) Dawson into the attack, there\u2019s plenty of head scratching out in the middle as the ball appears to clip the stumps when Nissanka misses a sweep shot but the bails stay on and the ball dribbles away for four byes! Someone\u2019s UHU\u2019d the bails Guv! Nissanka is looking imperious, he makes room to cut Dawson for four and then ends the over with wonderful lofted SIX over mid-off. Ffity up for Sri Lanka \u2013 they are going at ten an over. Even I can do that maths. 4th over: Sri Lanka 36-1 (Nissanka 11, Mendis 6) Nissanka attempts a paddle sweet to Archer which I\u2019m not sure is the wisest move. He misses the ball and is smashed on the pad, Archer pleads with the umpire who says not out and Harry Brook decides against sending it upstairs, wisely as it hit Nissanka outside the line. Nissanka is a joy to watch though, he trots down and lofts Archer over cover for four. A single brings Mendis on strike, he rocks back and unleashes a cut past backward point for four more. Decent start from the home side. 3rd over: Sri Lanka 25-1 ( Mishara 10, Nissanka 6) Kusal Mendis is the new batter, Overton keeps him honest with four dots. Seven runs and the wicket off the over. Jamie Overton replaces Curran and is immediately mullered into the stands over long-on by Mishara. That was some strike. Gone! Mishar tries to repeat the stroke but hits it straight up up and up. Liam Dawson takes a simple catch\u2026 did I mention how safe his hands were? England get their first. 2nd over: Sri Lanka 18-0 ( Mishara 10, Nissanka 6) Jofra Archer starts from t\u2019other end. He skims one past the outside edge of Mishara\u2019s bat and looks in fine fettle in his first few balls. DROP! Archer shows his frustration as Liam Dawson shells a chance at midwicket, Mishara given a life. Dawson was almost at full stretch but got there with his left hand and perhaps could have taken it he\u2019d gone with both. Just two off the over but a missed opportunity for England. I don\u2019t want to do Dawson down, but I recall seeing him drop quite a few catches in an England shirt now? Harsh but fair? 1st over: Sri Lanka 16-0 ( Mishara 9, Nissanka 5) The sky is bruised and so are Sam Curran\u2019s figures after just one over, the wee man is flogged for 16 runs off his first including three fours from over pitched deliveries that are given the treatment. Nissanka plays the pick of them with a languid cover drive that threads the field but Mishara didn\u2019t miss out either, picking off two boundaries through the off side with sweet timing. Sam Curran is going to start with the new ball for England. Let\u2019s play! Here are the teams: Sri Lanka: 1 Pathum Nissanka, 2 Kamil Mishara, 3 Kusal Mendis, 4 Dhananjaya de Silva, 5 Charith Asalanka, 6 Dasun Shanaka (c), 7 Janith Liyanage, 8 Wanindu Hasaranga, 9 Maheesh Theekshana, 10 Matheesha Pathirana, 11 Eshan Malinga England: 1 Phil Salt, 2 Jos Buttler (wk), 3 Jacob Bethell, 4 Tom Banton, 5 Harry Brook (c), 6 Sam Curran, 7 Will Jacks, 8 Jamie Overton, 9 Liam Dawson, 10 Jofra Archer, 11 Adil Rashid Taha chirps up from the ground and says he doesn\u2019t think there will be any more rain. Wahey. He also informs me that he has purchased three Sri Lanka floppy hats in the rain delay and that Paolo Nutini\u2019s \u2018Candy\u2019 was on his Spotify most played for 2022. He\u2019s like Alan Whicker. Crucially he\u2019s no longer Under an Iron Sky in Kandy. We\u2019ll have play in just a couple of minutes. Harry Brook calls the coin correctly at a soggy looking Pallekele, England choose to chase. No brainer. Here we go \u2013 official news of a toss in fifteen minutes (2.55pm) and a 3.10pm start. Still no news on an inspection or toss time from the ground, as soon as I get some intel you\u2019ll be the first to know. Why not quiz while we wait? Stand by your beds! The covers are being peeled off in Pallekele. No news is probably bad news I\u2019m afraid. There is some epic sport taking place right now though and I don\u2019t mean my elite oeuf scrambling. Djokovic and Sinner are locked in a fifth set over in Melbourne in the men\u2019s Aussie Open semi final. If Djokovic gets there he\u2019ll be the oldest in open era to do so, if he wins the thing then it\u2019ll be his much coveted 25th Grand Slam title. I mean, the guy is ancient \u2013 38 years old. Thirty Eight. (Ahem). Katy Murrells is on the tools for us here: The tarpaulins have been hauled on, which is not good. The whole outfield is now covered and steady rain is falling. So confident am I that we aren\u2019t going to get an update any time soon that I\u2019m off to pad into the kitchen and scramble some eggs. Before I crack into some Burford Brown\u2019s (very Guardian?) wait a minute, where\u2019s Rooty? Further bad news, the rain has returned and the covers are being pulled back on in Kandy. We await official news\u2026 In the meantime, here\u2019s Taha on a sorry tale: Gah. Spoke too soon, the toss is delayed by fifteen minutes while the ground staff complete some clean up. Never mind, we have plenty of pre-match reading for you to get stuck into. Not all of it that uplifting, mind. The good news is that the toss is about to happen and we should be underway on time. Taha Hashim is our man at the ground, he\u2019s been covering Jofra\u2019s return and speaking to another player to return to the T20 fold \u2013 Phil Salt: Hello and welcome to the first of three T20 Internationals between Sri Lanka and England from Kandy. After pulling off a series win in the longer stuff Harry Brook and his men are now getting down to brass tacks with the shorter format. The T20 World Cup starts in a little over a week and these matches are the final tune up, after a disastrous Ashes campaign it is fair to say that higher level jobs are in the spotlight and immediate futures will likely hinge on how England perform in the tournament. Some good news \u2013 Jofra Archer is back ahead of schedule after pulling his side in Australia, he wasn\u2019t initially named in the squad to play these matches but his early return is a boon for Harry Brook. Play will begin at 1.30pm GMT all being well, there are reports of some inclement weather in Kandy at the moment, whether the players are perched on the ground in the pouring rain, trying to make themselves a sail\u2026 remains to be seen. I\u2019ll be here OBOing for ya.",

                "webPublicationDate": "2026-01-30T18:29:19Z",
                "webTitle": "Catherine O\u2019Hara, actor known for Home Alone and Schitt\u2019s Creek, dies aged 71",
                "webUrl": "https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/jan/30/catherine-o-hara-dead-actor-home-alone",
                "apiUrl": "https://content.guardianapis.com/film/2026/jan/30/catherine-o-hara-dead-actor-home-alone",
                "fields": {
                    "headline": "Catherine O\u2019Hara, actor known for Home Alone and Schitt\u2019s Creek, dies aged 71",
                    "standfirst": "
Actor, also known for Beetlejuice and her work with Christopher Guest, died after a brief illness
  • Catherine O\u2019Hara managed to make difficult characters utterly delightul
  • Catherine O\u2019Hara: a life in pictures
",
                    "trailText": "Actor, also known for Beetlejuice and her work with Christopher Guest, died after a brief illness",
                    "byline": "Benjamin Lee",
                    "main": "",
                    "body": "
Catherine O\u2019Hara, actor known for Schitt\u2019s Creek, Home Alone and Best in Show, has died at the age of 71.
 
Her manager confirmed the news to Variety. She died after a brief illness.
 
O\u2019Hara started her comedy career in the 1970s and helped to create the Canadian sketch show SCTV. She broke into film in the 1980s with her first big-screen credit in the romantic comedy Nothing Personal with Donald Sutherland, and in 1985 she had a role in Martin Scorsese\u2019s black comedy After Hours.
 
 
 Related: Catherine O\u2019Hara managed to make difficult characters utterly delightul 
 
  
In 1988, O\u2019Hara starred in Tim Burton\u2019s comedy horror Beetlejuice and later reprised the role in the 2024 sequel. On the set of the original, she met her husband, production designer Bo Welch, and they married in 1992.
 
O\u2019Hara played Macaulay Culkin\u2019s careless mother in the smash hit 1990 comedy Home Alone, a role she also reprised for the 1992 sequel.
 
\u201cIt\u2019s a perfect movie, isn\u2019t it?\u201d she said of Home Alone to People in 2024. She added, of the experience: \u201cIt was lovely. All those kids that played our children were just lovely.\u201d
 
O\u2019Hara recently appeared at Culkin\u2019s Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony, wiping away tears as she praised him.
 
Culkin paid tribute to O\u2019Hara on Instagram, writing: \u201cMama. I thought we had time. I wanted more. I wanted to sit in a chair next to you. I heard you but I had so much more to say. I love you. I\u2019ll see you later.\u201d
 
She began working with Christopher Guest in 1996, starring in the mockumentary Waiting for Guffman, and starred in three more of his films: Best in Show, A Mighty Wind and For Your Consideration in 2006.
 
Guest praised O\u2019Hara for her ability to master comedy and drama in their last collaboration together. \u201cCatherine is one of not many actresses that can pull off both sides of this, where she\u2019s incredibly funny but can also shift into an emotional area that surprises people and it\u2019s just amazing, that transition,\u201d he said.
 
 
 Related: Catherine O\u2019Hara: a life in pictures 
 
  
O\u2019Hara also provided her voice for many animated films including Chicken Little, Over the Hedge, Monster House, Frankenweenie and, most recently, The Wild Robot.
    
On the small screen, she had roles in The Larry Sanders Show, Six Feet Under, Curb Your Enthusiasm and 30 Rock before she reunited with another Guest actor, Eugene Levy, for the hit sitcom Schitt\u2019s Creek.
 
\u201cIt\u2019s always more fun working with someone you know,\u201d she said to the Guardian in 2021. \u201cI get too nervous doing solo bits \u2013 it\u2019s too much pressure and it feels like showing off. With someone else, you can share the showing off.\u201d
 
The show, about a wealthy family who are forced to downsize, ran for six seasons and won O\u2019Hara an Emmy award.
 
Her recent television roles also included A Series of Unfortunate Events and The Last of Us, which scored her an Emmy nomination.
 
Her Last of Us co-star Pedro Pascal paid tribute on Instagram. \u201cOh, genius to be near you,\u201d he wrote. \u201cEternally grateful. There is less light in my world, this lucky world that had you, will keep you, always.\u201d
 
O\u2019Hara had recently been seen in the award-winning comedy series The Studio with Seth Rogen. The role had garnered her Emmy and Golden Globe nominations.
 
 
 Related: Catherine O\u2019Hara on the joy of Schitt\u2019s Creek: \u2018Eugene Levy is the sweetest man!\u2019 
 
  
Ron Howard, who directed O\u2019Hara in the 1992 comedy drama The Paper, paid his respects on social media.
 
\u201cThis is shattering news,\u201d he wrote. \u201cWhat a wonderful person, artist and collaborator. I was lucky enough to direct, produce and act in projects with her and she was simply growing more brilliant with each year.\u201d
 
Meryl Streep, who starred in Heartburn with O\u2019Hara, also shared a statement: \u201cCatherine O\u2019Hara brought love and light to our world, through whipsmart compassion for the collection of eccentrics she portrayed ... such a loss for her family and friends, and the audience she graced as friends.\u201d
 
Rita Wilson also called her \u201cauthentic and truthful in all she did\u201d on Instagram while Lily Tomlin wrote \u201cbright, beautiful, and full of joy that touched so many\u201d next to a picture of O\u2019Hara.
 
Mike Myers shared with the Hollywood Reporter: \u201cIt is a very sad day for comedy and for Canada. She was one of the greatest comedy artists in history, an inspiration for millions and above all a very elegant lady. Sending much love and condolences to her family.\u201d
 
\u201cI\u2019m always drawn to characters who have no idea of the impression they\u2019re making on other people,\u201d O\u2019Hara said in 2021. \u201cWe\u2019re all delusional, really, and I love that about us humans and I love playing it.\u201d
",

                "id": "sport/2026/jan/30/sri-lanka-england-cricket-first-t20-match-report",
                "type": "article",
                "sectionId": "sport",
                "sectionName": "Sport",
                "webPublicationDate": "2026-01-30T18:20:40Z",
                "webTitle": "Sam Curran takes hat-trick before Salt eases England to DLS win over Sri Lanka in first T20",
                "webUrl": "https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/jan/30/sri-lanka-england-cricket-first-t20-match-report",
                "apiUrl": "https://content.guardianapis.com/sport/2026/jan/30/sri-lanka-england-cricket-first-t20-match-report",
                "fields": {
                    "headline": "Sam Curran takes hat-trick before Salt eases England to DLS win over Sri Lanka in first T20",
                    "standfirst": "
  • 1st T20: England, 125-4, bt Sri Lanka, 133, by 11 runs (DLS)
  • Opener hits 46 as tourists win after rain delay
",
                    "trailText": "The seamer claimed three wickets after Adil Rashid, with three for 19, impressed in the opening Twenty20 in a rain-affected match",
                    "byline": "Taha Hashim at Pallekele Cricket Stadium",
                    "main": "",
                    "body": "
It was an England victory set up by the wily, age-old brilliance of Adil Rashid, vital to their hopes of a World Cup triumph in the coming weeks. The masterful leg-spinner took three for 19 as Sri Lanka\u2019s batting lineup collapsed in the first of three Twenty20s, losing five wickets for 22 runs.
 
Sam Curran celebrated a late \u00adhat-trick, too, as the visitors were set a target of 134 in a rain-shortened contest after the start was delayed. They were guided by Phil Salt\u2019s 46, but Tom Banton\u2019s 15-ball 29 provided the real thrust, easing the tension in the middle overs.
 
 
 Related: Harry Brook adds to England woes by admitting he lied about nightclub incident 
 
  
England were just about stumbling over the line when the rain returned with nine needed off 12 balls, the crowd filtering out before the official decision. Harry Brook\u2019s side lead the series after winning by 11 runs on DLS, but the joy will be limited among the tourists. In a statement released by Brook after the match he admitted he was with teammates on the night of his bouncer altercation in New Zealand. The fallout refuses to stop.
 
The Pallekele International Cricket Stadium \u2013 the venue for this entire 20-over series \u2013 was a lush sight before the start: green banks flank the field, screensaver hills dominate the backdrop. But unseasonal rain complicated things, chalking off six overs before the first ball.
 
England had named their XI the night before, including the fit-again Jofra Archer for his first appearance since the third Test of the Ashes. Brook chose to bowl first, gave his premier quick the second over, and there were positive signs after a month away: Archer began with a toe-hunter, got the ball leaping past Kamil Mishara\u2019s outside edge and nearly had the left-hander caught at midwicket, the leaping Liam Dawson unable to hold on.
 
But the opening passage belonged to Sri Lanka, with Curran struggling to find the right spot. After conceding 16 off the first over of the innings, he returned for the seventh and was laid into by Kusal Mendis for 20 more. Even the left-armer\u2019s new weapon, the moon ball, did not bring joy, Mendis sending a 50mph change-up down the ground for six.
 
As ever, England looked to Rashid for some beard-stroking wisdom. He combined with Dawson\u2019s twirl to ignite the middle-order implosion: 76 for one became 98 for six. Rashid looped the ball up to invite three fatal slogs, but his working over of Dhananjaya de Silva, dismissed for 11, was the standout. The 37-year-old began his final over with three dots as De Silva failed to decode the googly. A mistimed sweep to Curran in the deep followed.
    
Dasun Shanaka, Sri Lanka\u2019s recently reappointed T20 captain, provided some resistance with his 20, but Curran returned to rewrite the tune of his day. Shanaka and Maheesh Theekshana failed to clear the boundary when going down the ground before Curran went full, straight and lit up Matheesha Pathirana\u2019s stumps. The Surrey all-rounder conceded his runs at close to 13 an over; he also became the second man to take a T20 hat-trick for England, after Chris \u00adJordan in the 2024 World Cup.
 
This was Salt\u2019s first time taking on Sri Lanka, a surprising stat for an opener with more than 80 caps for England, but he was his usual self, bludgeoning Theekshana\u2019s box of tricks for 14 off his first three \u00addeliveries. As Jos Buttler began Eshan Malinga\u2019s first over with four consecutive boundaries, it seemed England were on for a quick one. But Malinga replied with a delicious variation, his off-cutter hanging in the air to bowl Buttler.
 
Jacob Bethell advanced to nine before he was also undone by Malinga\u2019s change of pace, the slower ball chipped to extra cover. When Salt, on 17, swatted Wanindu Hasaranga towards deep midwicket, the collapse seemed to be on. But Mishara spilled a simple chance and Banton calmed the situation in his first innings of the tour, punishing Hasaranga with consecutive reverse-slaps, the first for four, the second travelling all the way. The Somerset batter\u2019s takedown was key in leaving a simple equation at the drinks break, with 48 required off the last 48 balls.
 
Banton could not finish the job, smashing the impressive Pathirana to cover, and Brook was suddenly exposed, Hasaranga\u2019s googly not letting him settle. But Sri Lanka\u2019s clinical touch was missing, Pathirana denied the wicket of Brook when another catch went down, this time at deep cover. The slingy right-arm quick conceded just 18 off his four overs, setting his marker for the next two games. But Sri Lanka\u2019s errors in the field proved costly.

                "webPublicationDate": "2026-01-30T18:15:40Z",
                "webTitle": "Goodreads, but make it mindful: why I switched to a reading journal",
                "webUrl": "https://www.theguardian.com/thefilter-us/2026/jan/30/papier-reading-journal",
                "apiUrl": "https://content.guardianapis.com/thefilter-us/2026/jan/30/papier-reading-journal",
                "fields": {
                    "headline": "A reading journal won\u2019t make you smarter, but it will make you more mindful",
                    "standfirst": "
Papier\u2019s reading journal is the low-tech way I made reading feel calmer and more intentional \u2013 and you don\u2019t need to love reading to benefit from it
  • The best e-readers in the US, for every kind of book lover
  • 10 banned books for curious and rebellious US readers
  • Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things
",
                    "trailText": "Papier\u2019s reading journal is the low-tech way I made reading feel calmer and more intentional \u2013 and you don\u2019t need to love reading to benefit from it",
                    "byline": "Lauren Gould",
                    "main": "",
                    "body": "
In 2025, I thought I failed. I was six books shy of achieving my annual reading goal. No matter that I\u2019d read 44 books, more than the average American; it wasn\u2019t the 50 I\u2019d set out to complete.
 
For a while, flipping the pages of a novel has felt more like an item on my to-do list and less like a way to unwind. Then, while reporting on the best ways to read more in 2026 (are we surprised?), I tried out a reading journal from one of my favorite stationery brands, Papier.
 
I\u2019ve found the journal to be a structured, scrapbook-y way to keep track of my goals \u2013 and a way to transform reading into a more mindful and intentional experience.
 
Avid readers or not, we could probably all appreciate slowing down that way in our busy lives.
 
At a glance
 
     
  • The best way to read mindfully: Papier Reading Journal
    •  
   $32 at Revolve    $32.30 at Papier   
***
 
What exactly is a reading journal?
    
A reading journal is akin to a diary, but instead of recording your deepest thoughts (although those are welcome too), you\u2019re reflecting on what you\u2019re reading.
 
Sure, you can use Goodreads, but if you\u2019re trying to reduce your screentime, a reading journal is ideal. After trying Papier\u2019s, I can say it offers the same level of organization in a much more mindful package.
 
***
 
What\u2019s the best reading journal?
 
While plenty of stationary brands offer their own versions, I adore this beautifully designed one from Papier. In January, it helped me log six new reads. While this may read like sponsored content, I simply can\u2019t resist these journals that make me feel like I have my life together. I already swear by its daily planners.
    
The journal has an index with slots to record 32 books and their titles, genres, dates read and starred ratings. It also allots four pages per book for writing lengthier reviews. Rather than leave you puzzling over how to fill the space, each page has questions to guide your thoughts. A couple of my favorites: \u201cFirst impressions?\u201d and \u201cWould you read this book again?\u201d There\u2019s leftover space to write extra thoughts, favorite quotes and quick summaries.
    
The \u201cwishlist\u201d section lets me record up to 56 books I hope to add to my shelf. I\u2019ve already jotted down 12 novels, including two of my most anticipated releases, The Burning Side and Yesteryear. And as someone notorious for losing library books (and getting fined), I appreciate the \u201cborrowing and lending\u201d section, where I can log the loan and return dates for up to 25 titles.
 
***
 
How does it help both readers and non-readers?
    
In a culture that prioritizes productivity hacks and optimization, using a physical reading journal encouraged me to implement mindfulness into each reading session \u2013 and in turn, my everyday routine.
 
Knowing that I\u2019d have the opportunity to write an in-depth review and list my favorite quotes inspired me to slow down and reflect on each chapter, which is something I don\u2019t do enough of in my daily life.
 
And it\u2019s a chance to write your unfiltered thoughts on a book. In my Goodreads reviews, I found myself exercising caution, worrying about someone judging my scathing review of BookTok\u2019s latest romantasy fixation. However, in my journal, I didn\u2019t have to sugarcoat my feelings, making each review feel more genuine. I\u2019m often recruited by my busy corporate mom to select her next read, and I\u2019ve already used notes from past reviews to help me select a title I think she\u2019ll devour. (All the Little Houses, if you\u2019re curious.)
 
***
 
Can a reading journal really make you a better reader?
 
Realistically, a reading journal can\u2019t promise to take you from completing one book a year to 100. It can\u2019t promise to improve your vocabulary or double your reading speed. But what it can do is make reading a more mindful experience.
 
What\u2019s more, as someone prone to nostalgia, I love that my reading journal doubles as a physical keepsake. I\u2019m already looking forward to flipping through its pages in the years to come, when I can revisit my feelings about a book\u2019s themes and reflect on my most loved titles of the year \u2013 whether that be five or 50.
 
Papier Reading Journal
   $32 at Revolve    $32.30 at Papier ",

In my Goodreads reviews, I found myself exercising caution, worrying about someone judging my scathing review of BookTok\u2019s latest romantasy fixation. However, in my journal, I didn\u2019t have to sugarcoat my feelings, making each review feel more genuine. I\u2019m often recruited by my busy corporate mom to select her next read, and I\u2019ve already used notes from past reviews to help me select a title I think she\u2019ll devour. (All the Little Houses, if you\u2019re curious.) *** Can a reading journal really make you a better reader? Realistically, a reading journal can\u2019t promise to take you from completing one book a year to 100. It can\u2019t promise to improve your vocabulary or double your reading speed. But what it can do is make reading a more mindful experience. What\u2019s more, as someone prone to nostalgia, I love that my reading journal doubles as a physical keepsake. I\u2019m already looking forward to flipping through its pages in the years to come, when I can revisit my feelings about a book\u2019s themes and reflect on my most loved titles of the year \u2013 whether that be five or 50. Papier Reading Journal $32 at Revolve $32.30 at Papier",

                "webTitle": "Attorney general defends missing Congress deadline \u2013 as it happened",
                "webUrl": "https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/jan/30/donald-trump-immigration-ice-iran-kevin-warsh-us-politics-live-news-updates",
